+# Triangle Multiplicative Update (SM100 / SM103 / SM107)
+
+**This is an experimental API and subject to change.**
+
+## Overview
+
+`cudnn.triangle_multiplicative_update` is the AlphaFold-class triangle multiplicative update ("outgoing" / "incoming"
+triangle multiplication, AlphaFold 3 Algorithms 12 and 13) as three FROST CuTe-DSL launches on one stream, behind the
+signature of `cuequivariance_ops_torch.triangle_multiplicative_update` (pinned to cuequivariance-ops-torch **0.12.0**:
+the same parameter names, order and defaults, so a model switches providers by changing one import).
+
+```text
+x [B, N, N, c_z] bf16   (the pair representation; the caller adds the residual to the result)
+ |
+ |  K1  LayerNorm_in over the channel, the gated dual projections (value || gate) for a and b, sigmoid * mul, the pair mask
+ |      -> a, b   channel-major planes [c, B*N, n_pad] bf16                      LayerNorm-prologue dual GEMM (FROST)
+ |  K2  the per-channel contraction   y[c][i, j] = sum_k a[c][i, k] b[c][j, k]   (outgoing)   /   sum_k a[c][k, i] b[c][k, j]   (incoming)
+ |      -> y      channel-major [c, B*N, n_pad] bf16                             ONE batched GEMM (batch = c * B) on the FROST GEMM engine
+ |  K3  LayerNorm_out over the channel of y, LayerNorm_in of x recomputed, output projection * sigmoid(output gate)
+ v      -> out    pair-major [B, N, N, c_z] bf16
+```
+
+Every stage is a FROST kernel; there are no cuBLAS or cuDNN-backend call-outs. K1 and K3 are the two arms of one
+LayerNorm-prologue dual-GEMM body (`cudnn.gemm.frost.ln_prologue`), K2 is the shipped FROST GEMM template compiled for the
+contraction's tile (chosen per N from a measured prototype). The intermediate planes and `y` live in one workspace the
+caller provides (class API) or the function allocates (drop-in).
+
+**Target: NVIDIA Rubin (SM107, compute capability 10.7) and NVIDIA Blackwell (SM100 / SM103, compute capability 10.0 / 10.3).**
+The three kernels are the same code on both: the LayerNorm-prologue dual-GEMM body is rendered once per architecture family at the
+part's geometry (Rubin: a 9-deep operand ring in the 327 KiB carveout, 576 TMEM columns; Blackwell: a 6-deep ring -- 4 in the output
+stage -- in the 227 KiB opt-in carveout, 512 TMEM columns, so `c_z = 256` fills the output stage's ring exactly), and the contraction's
+FROST GEMM template sizes its pipeline from the live device. Every other architecture is declined with a typed error
+(`NotImplementedError`), never served slowly. The measured performance below is Rubin's; the Blackwell column of the heuristics is its own
+measured table (every knob swept on a GB200, 152 SMs at a 1830 MHz lock, by the same protocol; the `N < 256` buckets carry the Rubin picks
+until measured there).
+
+## Mathematics and numerics
+
+For every pair `(i, j)` of a batch entry, with `c_z` the pair width, `c` the hidden width, `m` the pair mask (`None` = all valid):
+
+```text
+z_in = LayerNorm_{c_z}(x; norm_in_weight, norm_in_bias, eps)
+a    = sigmoid(z_in . g_in_weight[:c]^T + g_in_bias[:c]) * (z_in . p_in_weight[:c]^T + p_in_bias[:c]) * m
+b    = sigmoid(z_in . g_in_weight[c:]^T + g_in_bias[c:]) * (z_in . p_in_weight[c:]^T + p_in_bias[c:]) * m
+y    = einsum("bikc,bjkc->bijc", a, b)   (outgoing)      /      einsum("bkic,bkjc->bijc", a, b)   (incoming)
+u    = LayerNorm_c(y; norm_out_weight, norm_out_bias, eps)
+out  = sigmoid(z_in . g_out_weight^T + g_out_bias) * (u . p_out_weight^T + p_out_bias)
+```
+
+Parameter conventions are cuEquivariance's: `p_in_weight`, `g_in_weight` are `[2 c, c_z]` with rows `[a; b]`; `p_out_weight`
+is `[c_z, c]`; `g_out_weight` is `[c_z, c_z]`; the LayerNorm vectors are `[c_z]` (in) and `[c]` (out); every bias is optional
+(`None` = zero). The output is not masked (the mask acts on `a` and `b`), and the residual add is the caller's.
+
+Rounding points (all arithmetic fp32 with bf16 storage): LayerNorm statistics in fp32 (two-pass), the LayerNormed operand rounded
+once to bf16 as the MMA operand; `a` and `b` rounded once to bf16 **after** the mask multiplies in fp32 (a zero mask row is exactly
+`+0.0`; cuEquivariance multiplies a bf16-rounded product -- identical for `{0, 1}` and power-of-two masks, one bf16 ulp apart on
+fractional weights); `y` accumulated in fp32 and rounded once to bf16; the gate sigmoid through `tanh.approx`; the output rounded
+once to bf16. `cudnn.triangle_multiplicative_update.triangle_multiplicative_update_reference` is the fp64 reference with these
+rounding points inserted (`rounding="kernel"`) or without them (`rounding="none"`, the pure formula). Measured on the test grid
+(N in 64..768, both directions, masks all / padded / random, biases on and off): relative RMS to the kernel-rounding reference
+1.68e-3 (= the output's bf16 rounding alone); per cell `|diff| <= 4e-3 + |ref| / 64` on all but 0.7..7.6 per million cells, every
+cell within `2e-2 + |ref| / 64` (the tail of bf16 rounding flips propagating through the contraction); relative RMS to the
+unrounded fp64 formula below 2e-2.
+
+## Served today, and the typed declines
+
+| what | served | otherwise |
+|---|---|---|
+| architecture | compute capability 10.7 (Rubin), 10.0 / 10.3 (Blackwell SM100 / SM103) | `NotImplementedError` |
+| dtype | bf16 pair representation, bf16 parameters (`precision='bfloat16'` casts wider inputs once per call, as cuEquivariance does) | `NotImplementedError` |
+| pair width `c_z` / hidden width `c` | `c_z == c` in `{128, 256}` (`c_z % 32 != 0` is a `ValueError`: cuEquivariance's own rule); 384 is withdrawn until its renderings stop spilling and carry an oracle cell. 256 is served correctly but not yet competitively (13-44 % behind cuEquivariance's generic route at N >= 217: the measured-performance section) | `NotImplementedError` |
+| N | `N >= 33`, any N for the outgoing direction; the incoming direction needs `N % 8 == 0` | `NotImplementedError` |
+| direction | `"outgoing"`, `"incoming"` | `ValueError` |
+| mask | `None`, or `[B, N, N]` (`[N, N]` for B = 1) of any real / bool dtype (cast once per call to bf16 when not already bf16 contiguous) | `ValueError` on a shape mismatch |
+| `precision` | `None` / `'default'` / `'none'` / `'bfloat16'` (`'bf16'`) | `'mxfp8'`, `'ieee'`, `'tf32'`: `NotImplementedError` |
+| parameters | the eight weights are required (no implicit initialisation); biases optional | `ValueError` |
+| layout | contiguous `x` (and `out`) | `ValueError` (never a hidden copy) |
+| aliasing | `out` and the workspace disjoint, as byte ranges, from every tensor the kernels read (`x`, the mask, the parameters) and from each other -- two views over one allocation whose ranges intersect are declined, pointer inequality is not enough (the output stage reads `x` while it writes `out`) | `ValueError` naming the two operands, before any launch |
+| tensor extent | `B*N*N*c_z` and `2*c*B*N*n_pad` below 2^31 (32-bit element offsets in the kernels) | `NotImplementedError` |
+| device | every `execute` tensor on the device the plan was declared on | `ValueError` |
+| performance knobs | `k2_tile` / `knobs=TriMulKnobs(...)` within the measured domains of `cudnn.triangle_multiplicative_update.heuristics` (contraction tile, projection tile order, output-stage prologue form, scheduler ring depth, row tile, LayerNorm pass form, epilogue arithmetic form, the two stages' `.minnctapersm` register-split hint) -- every value computes the same function | `ValueError` on an unknown name; `NotImplementedError` when the contraction tile cannot serve the geometry on this device |
+| autograd | not registered yet (forward only); under `torch.no_grad()` or on detached tensors the call is served | `NotImplementedError` when grad mode is on and an input or parameter `requires_grad` (a tensor without `grad_fn` would silently drop the gradient) |
+
+The `c != c_z` geometries (Protenix-v2 style), `c_z` outside the two widths, N below 33 and the incoming direction at `N % 8 != 0`
+are the current kernel envelope, not the operation's; each is a typed decline naming the rule.
+
+## Drop-in function
+
+```python
+import cudnn
+from cudnn import triangle_multiplicative_update   # or: from cuequivariance_torch import triangle_multiplicative_update
+
+out = triangle_multiplicative_update(
+    x, "outgoing", mask,
+    norm_in_weight, norm_in_bias, p_in_weight, p_in_bias, g_in_weight, g_in_bias,
+    norm_out_weight, norm_out_bias, p_out_weight, p_out_bias, g_out_weight, g_out_bias,
+    eps=1e-5, precision=None,
+)
+z = z + out                                        # the residual is the caller's, as with cuEquivariance
+```
+
+Signature (cuEquivariance 0.12.0, verbatim; the two keyword-only additions are appended):
+
+```python
+triangle_multiplicative_update(x, direction="outgoing", mask=None,
+                               norm_in_weight=None, norm_in_bias=None, p_in_weight=None, p_in_bias=None,
+                               g_in_weight=None, g_in_bias=None, norm_out_weight=None, norm_out_bias=None,
+                               p_out_weight=None, p_out_bias=None, g_out_weight=None, g_out_bias=None,
+                               eps=1e-5, precision=None, *, out=None, stream=None) -> torch.Tensor
+```
+
+`out` writes into a caller-provided bf16 tensor (stable addresses for CUDA-graph users): `[B, N, N, c_z]`, or `[N, N, c_z]` at `B = 1`,
+contiguous, its bytes disjoint from `x`, the mask, every parameter and the workspace (an intersecting byte range is a typed
+`ValueError` before any launch); it is returned as given, whatever its rank -- only an output the function allocated follows `x`'s rank.
+`stream` is a raw CUDA stream handle the
+allocations and launches are ordered on (`None` = torch's current stream). The function caches one compiled plan per
+`(shape, direction, mask present, biases present, eps)` and one prepared parameter set per parameter identity (address, shape,
+strides, dtype, device, in-place version counter; a bounded LRU), allocates the output and the workspace per call, and launches.
+Parameters created under `torch.inference_mode()` carry no version counter and bypass that cache: they are prepared on every call
+(an in-place update of such a parameter could not be tracked) -- create them outside inference mode, or prepare them once with
+`prepare_weights` and use the class API, to pay the interleave once.
+Warm a shape once before capturing a `torch.cuda.graph` around the call; the captured graph replays the three kernels and follows
+the inputs' contents.
+
+## Prepared class API
+
+```python
+from cudnn.triangle_multiplicative_update import TriangleMultiplicativeUpdateFwd, prepare_weights
+
+weights = prepare_weights(norm_in_weight, norm_in_bias, p_in_weight, p_in_bias, g_in_weight, g_in_bias,
+                          norm_out_weight, norm_out_bias, p_out_weight, p_out_bias, g_out_weight, g_out_bias)   # once per parameter set
+plan = TriangleMultiplicativeUpdateFwd(x, "outgoing", c_hidden=128, has_mask=True, has_in_bias=True, has_out_bias=True)
+plan.check_support()                       # typed declines
+plan.compile()                             # K1, K2 (per-N tile), K3 -- cached per parameter set across instances
+workspace = torch.empty(plan.get_workspace_size(), dtype=torch.uint8, device=x.device)
+out = torch.empty_like(x)
+plan.execute(x, mask, weights, out, workspace, current_stream=None)   # validates and launches; no allocation, no sync
+graph = plan.make_cuda_graph(x, mask, weights, out, workspace)        # optional: one graph launch per call for these buffers
+```
+
+`prepare_weights` turns cuEquivariance's parameters into the kernels' layouts once (the value / gate rows interleaved per
+128-channel block, the biases stacked; a bias given on one side only is paired with zeros here, never per call). The constructor
+accepts a tensor or a `cudnn.api_base.TensorDesc`; the declaration's flags are compile-time specialisations the `execute`
+arguments must match exactly (a mask passed to a plan compiled without one raises, and vice versa). `get_workspace_size()` is the
+two channel-major planes plus `y` (bf16, the inner axis padded to a multiple of 8, 256-byte aligned) plus a small readable slack the
+outgoing contraction over-reads at `N % 8 != 0`. The performance knobs come from `cudnn.triangle_multiplicative_update.heuristics`:
+`recommend(N, c, B, direction)` returns the measured default `TriMulKnobs` -- a bucket table keyed by (hidden width, N bucket) carries the
+complete knob set, and a short refinement table overrides one axis per (batch bucket, direction) where a measured cell beat the bucket's pick
+decisively in every pass that measured it. The bucket picks: the contraction tile (the 1-CTA 128x128 tile at N <= 128 and at 384, the 2-CTA
+pair tile at 129-256 and 768, with the A operand multicast across 2 CTAs at 512 and across 4 from 1024), the projection stage's tile order
+(`interleaved` at c = 128 below N = 512, `major` elsewhere), the output stage's prologue form (`transpose` at c = 128, `mn_major` at c = 256)
+and the scheduler ring depth (1 from N >= 384 at c = 128 and from N >= 129 at c = 256, else 2). The refinements: at c = 128 the ring is 1 deep
+at N <= 128 for the incoming direction with B = 1, 1 deep with the pass-major projection order at 256 <= N < 384 from B >= 4, and 4 deep at
+384 <= N < 512 with B = 1; at c = 256 the ring is 1 deep at N <= 128 from B >= 4. Batch sizes
+other than 1 and 4 take the nearest measured batch bucket below (B >= 4 -> the B = 4 picks, else the B = 1 picks), an N between two buckets
+the first bucket at or below it. Every pick is the best of a three-pass measured sweep on one GPU of a 212-SM Rubin perf node (both directions,
+B = 1 and 4, a control pair per cell; the second and third passes re-measured every alternative against the table they shipped). The
+constructor's `k2_tile=` (one axis) or `knobs=` (a `TriMulKnobs` whose set axes override the pick; an axis left `None` keeps the table's value)
+override it, `check_support` validates the vocabulary and probes the contraction tile's eligibility for the geometry without compiling. Every
+value of every domain computes the same function (bitwise; the tests pin it). One axis is not a geometry pick: `min_blocks_per_mp`, the two
+LayerNorm-prologue stages' `.minnctapersm` launch hint (0 = the rendering as shipped, whose register split ptxas drops; 1 = the hint under
+which ptxas honours it), is resolved per RENDERING by `heuristics.register_split_hint(stage, c, has_bias, ln_pass_form, epi_math, pass_order,
+ln_once)` from the measured rows -- whether a rendering spills at the flat allocation depends on its bias arm, its forms, the projection stage's
+tile order and the LayerNorm-once work item, not on N or B.  Every measured row names the per-tile item (`ln_once=""`); under the `"block"`
+item the table ships from N = 256 at c = 128 the hinted renderings spill and the hint measured a loss of 0.7..1.3 % on the whole call without
+the biases (neutral with them, on the 212-SM Rubin class), so those plans run unhinted -- and a `knobs=` value overrides it for both stages.
+The epilogue arithmetic form has a bias-path member, `epi_math="packed_biasfold"` (the gate bias staged
+halved and folded into the tanh argument's fused multiply-add: 16 fewer packed adds per 32-channel subtile per lane; output-bitwise the
+`packed` form, and byte-identical to it when the stage has no biases), which the table picks where the projection stage runs the register
+LayerNorm form at N >= 256 (+1.0..+1.7 % on the whole call with the biases on the 212-SM Rubin class; a rolled-form projection stage loses
+~0.7 % under it, so those cells keep `packed`); `"packed_hoist"` (the bias loads issued ahead of the TMEM loads) is admitted as a knob and
+measured neutral.
+

+## Experimental Python APIs
+
+**FE-OSS APIs are experimental and subject to change.**
+
+The GEMM CuTeDSL APIs are type-erased and torch-lazy: torch is imported only when torch tensors are passed. JAX arrays are additionally accepted wherever the kernel's tensor layouts are expressible as row-major arrays (each API's page has a "JAX support" section with its exact contract):
+
+- **Dense fusions** (amax, swiglu, srelu, dsrelu): full JAX eager support, plus `jax.jit`-compatible XLA custom-call entry points for all four (built on `cudnn.jax.call` / CuTeDSL's native `cutlass.jax` bridge; see `gemm_amax.md` "Using JAX arrays").
+- **Grouped / discrete-grouped**: JAX eager support in discrete (pointer-array) weight modes — unfused grouped GEMM, glu/dglu (BF16), dsrelu (FP8), wgrad (BF16), and discrete-grouped swiglu/dswiglu (FP8) — plus a `jax.jit`-compatible `*_jax_sm100` entry point for each of those same families (built on `cudnn.jax.call`; each API page documents its exact jit contract). Contiguous grouped MXFP8 SwiGLU/dSwiGLU wrappers accept Torch tensors and canonical JAX arrays, including under `jax.jit`, with explicit FP8 output dtype and `sf_vec_size=32` for JAX. The unified GLU wrapper likewise dispatches canonical MXFP8 JAX inputs to `grouped_gemm_glu_jax_sm100` (SwiGLU/GeGLU), which runs the Rubin GLU kernel on SM107. The unified dGLU, wgrad and quant wrappers likewise dispatch canonical JAX inputs to `grouped_gemm_dglu_jax_sm100` (dSwiGLU/dGeGLU), `grouped_gemm_wgrad_jax_sm100` and `grouped_gemm_quant_jax_forward`, which run the Rubin kernels on SM107. The grouped SReLU, dSReLU, GLU+Hadamard and GLU+Hadamard+quant wrappers dispatch to `grouped_gemm_srelu_jax_forward`, `grouped_gemm_dsrelu_jax_sm100`, `grouped_gemm_glu_hadamard_jax_forward` and `grouped_gemm_glu_hadamard_quant_jax_forward` (SM100+, as in Torch; GLU+Hadamard+quant runs its Rubin kernel on SM107). These canonical entries take dense weights in MXFP8 or packed FP4 (as `uint8`, with E4M3 scales per 16 for NVFP4), and GLU, dGLU and wgrad also take BF16; each page lists its formats. Existing Torch behavior and wrapper defaults are unchanged. Discrete block-scaled weights, column-major bias layouts and the op classes reject JAX with clear errors.
+- **proj_rope_mxfp8**: JAX eager support on both input paths with `w_out_in=True` (the transposed [in, out] weight view is torch-only), plus the `jax.jit`-compatible `gemm_proj_rope_mxfp8_jax_sm100` entry point.

+New APIs follow the [Python API Naming Conventions](/operations/api_conventions).

+## Installation and setup
+
+All Frontend OSS APIs come installed with the `nvidia-cudnn-frontend` package. Except on Windows ARM64, `nvidia-cutlass-dsl[cu13]>=4.8.0` and `apache-tvm-ffi` are required dependencies, so the CuTeDSL runtime comes with the base install (and the DSL pulls `cuda-python` in transitively):
+```bash
+pip install nvidia-cudnn-frontend
+```
+On Windows ARM64, these two runtime dependencies are excluded from the base installation, so the base install does not enable the CuTeDSL APIs there.
+
+(`pip install nvidia-cudnn-frontend[cutedsl]` still works; the `cutedsl` extra now names only `cuda-python`. A few APIs still want extras of their own — the cuTile linear-attention engines need `[cutile]`.)
+
+The Triton NVFP4 attention QAT backward API additionally requires the
+`triton` extra. Its API page documents the framework and GPU requirements.
+
+Those required dependencies are framework-neutral. Install your tensor framework separately — from a checkout, the PEP 735 dependency groups pin the right companion packages:
+```bash
+pip install --group torch   # torch + torch-c-dlpack-ext
+pip install --group jax     # jax >= 0.5 (XLA entry points via cutlass.jax, shipped with nvidia-cutlass-dsl)
+```
+(For the published wheel, `pip install torch torch-c-dlpack-ext` or `pip install "jax>=0.5"` directly.)
+
+After installation, you can import the APIs directly from the `cudnn` package, i.e. `from cudnn import {your_operation}`
+
+## API Usage
+
+The causal-convolution family exposes semantic PyTorch operations only through
+`cudnn.ops.causal_conv1d` and `cudnn.ops.causal_conv1d_update`; they return
+ordinary tensors and keep prepared kernel objects private. The wrapper and
+class conventions below apply to prepared frontend-only kernel APIs.
+
+Most compiler-style operations expose the following two APIs. Functional
+autograd integrations such as BSA and Flex Attention instead document their
+own wrapper and reusable-plan lifecycle on their operation pages.
+
+### 1. High-level wrapper
+
+- Single pythonic function call
+- Allocates and returns output tensors
+- Returns outputs as a `TupleDict` (supports both dictionary-style key access and tuple unpacking)
+- No explicit compilation step – internally caches compiled kernels via a simple dictionary lookup
+- When to use:
+  - Fast prototyping and common cases
+  - You want automatic allocation and minimal boilerplate
+  - You are okay with the library managing the compiled-kernel cache
+
+```python
+from cudnn import {your_operation}_wrapper
+result = {your_operation}_wrapper(
+    inputs,
+    ...,
+    config_options,
+    ...,
+    stream=None,
+)
+
+# Dictionary-style access (recommended)
+primary_output = result["output_tensor_name"]
+
+# Tuple unpacking (order follows documented wrapper output keys)
+out0, out1 = result
+```
+
+### 2. Class API
+
+- Explicit lifecycle with compile and execute steps
+- Reusable object with underlying compiled kernel for multiple executions
+- Requires preallocated output tensors
+- When to use:
+  - You need to reuse a compiled kernel across many calls
+  - You want explicit control over compilation and lifecycle management
+  
+```python
+from cudnn import {your_operation}
+
+op = {your_operation}(
+    sample_inputs,
+    ...,
+    sample_outputs,
+    ...,
+    config_options,
+    ...
+)
+op.compile()
+op.execute(
+    inputs,
+    ...
+    outputs,
+    ...
+    current_stream=None,
+)
+```
+Methods:
+- `check_support()` – validates target problem configuration (i.e. tensor shapes, tensor strides, dtypes, tiling/cluster/kernel configurations, environment, etc.)
+- `compile()` – compiles the kernel with the provided sample tensors and parameters.
+- `execute(inputs, ..., outputs, ..., current_stream)` – runs the kernel with the provided inputs and outputs.
+  
+## Common Parameters and Conventions
+
+- CUDA stream (`current_stream` in class API, `stream` in wrapper)
+  - The cuda stream to use for operation kernel execution.
+  - Default: None (uses default stream)
+
+- Determinism
+  - Several kernels reduce with cross-CTA atomics, so those outputs are not bit-exact run to
+    run. Kernels react to `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)`: they switch to a
+    deterministic path where one exists, and otherwise raise (or warn, under
+    `warn_only`) rather than silently return a non-reproducible result.
+  - Where a deterministic path exists it can also be selected per call with
+    `deterministic=True`, independent of the torch setting. See
+    [Grouped GEMM + dsReLU](/operations/Matmul/gemm_fusions/grouped_gemm_dsrelu#deterministic-dprob).
+
+
+## File structure and examples
+
+- All FE OSS APIs are implemented in the `python/cudnn` directory.
+- Correctness tests/samples are implemented under `test/python/<operation>/cutedsl` (JAX bindings under `test/python/<operation>/jax`).

+# Block Sparse Attention (BSA)
+
+**This is an experimental API and subject to change.**
+
+## Overview
+
+Block Sparse Attention computes non-causal scaled dot-product attention over a
+block-level sparse pattern. For query token `i`, let `m = floor(i / block_size)`
+be its query-block index and let `K_m` be the union of the key/value blocks
+listed for that query block. The operation is
+
+$$
+O_i = \text{softmax}_{j \in K_m}
+\left(\frac{Q_i K_j^T}{\sqrt{D}}\right)V_j.
+$$
+
+The softmax is normalized once over all valid tokens in the selected blocks.
+`block_sizes` can shorten individual key/value blocks so that padded tokens do
+not participate in the softmax.
+
+Unlike [NSA Selection Attention](/operations/sparse_attention/nsa#1-selection-attention), BSA supplies one
+list of key/value blocks per **query block**. NSA Selection supplies routing
+metadata at query-token granularity and is one component of the larger NSA
+pipeline.
+
+BSA is implemented with Python CuTe DSL/JIT kernels.
+
+## Installation
+
+Except on Windows ARM64, the CuTe DSL runtime is a required dependency, so the base install is enough:
+
+```bash
+pip install nvidia-cudnn-frontend
+```
+
+On Windows ARM64, the CuTe DSL and TVM-FFI runtime dependencies are excluded from the base installation, so the base install does not enable BSA there.
+
+The package-wide `nvidia-cutlass-dsl[cu13]>=4.8.0` dependency floor applies to
+BSA. Sage FP8 relies on functionality introduced in CuTe DSL 4.6.1, which the
+package floor already satisfies. A defensive runtime check remains for
+environments that force an older DSL; the KPage path has the same check at
+the package floor and was verified on CuTe DSL 4.6.2, 4.7.0, and 4.7.1.
+
+## Forward
+
+```python
+import torch
+from cudnn.ops import (
+    block_sparse_attention_forward,
+    block_sparse_attention_backward,
+    block_sparse_attention_fp8_forward,
+)
+
+q = torch.randn(1, 8, 1024, 128, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+k = torch.randn(1, 8, 2048, 128, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+v = torch.randn_like(k)
+
+# For the SM90 blk64 path, this example has 16 Q blocks and 32 KV blocks.
+# Every Q block attends to the first four KV blocks.
+q2k_block_index = torch.arange(4, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+q2k_block_index = q2k_block_index.view(1, 1, 1, 4).expand(1, 8, 16, 4).contiguous()
+block_sizes = torch.full((32,), 64, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+
+result = block_sparse_attention_forward(
+    q,
+    k,
+    v,
+    q2k_block_index,
+    block_sparse_num=4,
+    block_sizes=block_sizes,
+    sparse_block_size=64,
+)
+o, lse = result
+# The same values are available as result["o_tensor"] and result["lse_tensor"].
+```
+
+The default layout is `BHSD`. Pass `layout="bshd"` for tensors in `BSHD`
+layout. The output follows the input layout, while `lse` is always the FP32
+natural-log log-sum-exp with shape `(B, H_q, S_q)`.
+
+For explicit Blackwell blk64 calls, TMA-aligned BSHD inputs are read through
+strided views. Both unsplit outputs and split-KV combined outputs are written
+directly in the requested layout. Misaligned inputs retain their staging fallback.
+
+### Sparse metadata
+
+| Argument | Shape | Dtype | Meaning |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| `q2k_block_index` | `(B, H_q, N_q, K_max)` | `int32` | KV-block IDs; only the valid prefix of each last dimension is read |
+| `block_sparse_num` | scalar | Python `int` | Fixed valid-prefix length for every query block |
+| `q2k_block_nums` | `(B, H_q, N_q)` | `int32` | Optional per-query-block valid-prefix lengths; overrides `block_sparse_num` |
+| `block_sizes` | `(N_kv,)` or backend-supported batched form | `int32` | Number of valid tokens in each KV block |
+
+Here `N_q = ceil(S_q / sparse_block_size)` and
+`N_kv = ceil(S_kv / sparse_block_size)`. Except for packed GQA described below,
+metadata is per query head. The metadata tensors must reside on the same CUDA
+device as `q`, `k`, and `v`. The value ranges below are a hard caller contract.
+
+#### Value ranges (caller contract)
+
+Let `K_max = q2k_block_index.shape[-1]`. Only the active prefix of each
+`q2k_block_index` row — the first `q2k_block_nums[b, h, m]` entries with
+variable counts, or the first `block_sparse_num` entries with a fixed count —
+is consumed. Values in the inactive suffix are ignored.
+
+- Within each row, active `q2k_block_index` values must be unique integers in
+  `[0, N_kv)`.
+- For forward with variable counts, every `q2k_block_nums` value must be in
+  `[0, K_max]` when `allow_empty_block_nums=True`, and in `[1, K_max]`
+  otherwise. Backward variable counts may be in `[0, K_max]`.
+- With fixed counts, `block_sparse_num` must be in `[1, K_max]`. The
+  FP16/BF16 SM100/SM103 blk128 path additionally requires an even value, i.e. an even
+  `block_sparse_num` in `[2, K_max]`.
+- The `block_sizes` entry for every physical KV block referenced by an active
+  `q2k_block_index` value must be in `[1, sparse_block_size]`. Entries for
+  unreferenced physical KV blocks are ignored. A zero-sized referenced block is
+  not supported by regular FP16/BF16 attention; use `q2k_block_nums` (or the
+  sparse index prefix) to drop the block instead. FP8 SM100/SM103 blk128 also
+  accepts zero-sized blocks, as specified in its architecture contract below.
+
+Tensor value ranges and per-row uniqueness are not validated at runtime.
+Violating the contract is unsupported and may produce invalid results or
+invalid device memory accesses.
+
+On the SM100/SM103 blk128 path, `pack_gqa=None` automatically packs GQA when
+the GQA ratio `r = H_q / H_kv` divides 128. Packed metadata has shape
+`(B, H_kv, ceil(S_q * r / 128), K_max)`. Pass `pack_gqa=False` to use the
+unpacked `(B, H_q, ceil(S_q / 128), K_max)` contract on every architecture.
+Explicit `pack_gqa=True` requires `r` to divide 128.
+
+When `block_sizes=None`, each referenced physical KV block is treated as full.
+Provide `block_sizes` whenever a referenced final block is only partially
+valid.
+
+`sparse_block_size=None` chooses blk64 on SM90/SM120 and blk128 on
+SM100/SM103. On SM90 or SM120, passing `sparse_block_size=128` selects a native
+KV128 kernel that consumes blk128 metadata directly; it does not
+expand the metadata or invoke the blk64 kernel. Passing `sparse_block_size=64`
+explicitly selects the SM100/SM103 blk64 CuTe DSL path, whose shape support is
+narrower. `kv_splits` is available on SM90 and the explicit Blackwell blk64
+path; `use_clc` applies only to the explicit Blackwell blk64 path.
+
+For SM120 blk128 with fixed `block_sparse_num`, full physical KV blocks
+(`block_sizes=None`), and a KV sequence length divisible by 128, the dispatcher
+uses an FA4-style native specialization with a dedicated K/V load warp,
+register-resident Q, and a four-fold-unrolled sparse loop. Most CTAs process
+128 Q rows; an underfilled final scheduling wave may use 64 Q rows per CTA
+while still loading full KV128 blocks and using the parent Q block's original
+metadata. This is Q-work scheduling, not KV128-to-KV64 lowering. Variable
+per-row block counts, explicit block sizes, and partial final KV blocks use
+the general native blk128 kernel. The FA4-style specialization requires
+`nvidia-cutlass-dsl >= 4.7.0`; an older public DSL version is rejected with
+a version-specific error before the specialized kernel is imported. The
+package-wide downstream dependency floor is unchanged.
+
+`kv_splits=2..256` computes FP32 partial outputs and combines them, with
+workspace growing linearly in the split count. SM90 accepts an explicit integer
+split count or `kv_splits="auto"` (the default stays 1). On SM90 the split
+count is chosen so one split's K/V region of a head fits in about 3/4 of L2:
+once a head's K/V exceeds L2 the unsplit kernel turns DRAM-bound, and a split
+grid orders every Q tile of one KV range before the next. The BF16/FP16 MHA
+policy applies at one head per wave (`ceil(S_q / 64)` at least `3 * SMs`), at most 25% density and fixed
+counts, and declines (one split) otherwise; it was measured on H100 with
+independent random indices (64 MiB K/V per head: 2 splits, +20%; 128 MiB: 4,
++70%; 256 MiB: 8, +94%; dense lists lose 12%). A caller-provided output
+also resolves to one split. The SM100/SM103 blk64 path also accepts `kv_splits="auto"`; CLC is
+compatible with split execution. Pass `use_clc=True` to use persistent CLC
+scheduling with `kv_splits>1`, or `use_clc=False` to use one tile per CTA. The
+default `use_clc=None` keeps CLC disabled for split execution because the
+automatic scheduler policy has not been tuned for that combination.
+
+The BF16 automatic policy is tuned assuming approximately uniform random KV
+indices with little overlap between the neighborhoods of different Q blocks.
+It uses host-visible tensor metadata and device properties, without reading
+indices or counts back to the host. Highly overlapping, shared or local-window
+indices can favor a different split count even at the same shape and density;
+benchmark explicit `kv_splits` values for those masks. This assumption affects
+performance only, not attention semantics or supported mask patterns.
+
+For fewer than 512 total Q tiles (`B * H * ceil(S_q / 64)`), the existing policy
+uses the fixed active block count, or index capacity for variable counts:
+256--449 blocks select two splits, 450--899 select four, and 900 or more select
+eight. Larger Q grids keep one split except in the measured long-Q region:
+BF16 MHA with Q/K/V head dimensions 128, `S_q >= 262144`, a fixed count of at
+least 512 active KV blocks, and density at most 1/8 (active blocks divided by
+`ceil(S_k / 64)`). In that region, K+V bytes **per batch and KV head** above twice
+the device L2 size select eight splits for at least 900 active blocks and four
+or more heads; a single head requires at least 1024 active blocks. Otherwise,
+four or more heads select four splits when per-head K+V bytes exceed L2.
+All other cases, including an unavailable L2 size, keep one split. Variable
+per-row counts also keep one split on larger Q grids because index capacity
+does not describe actual row work. The Sage FP8 policy is separate.
+
+Automatic selection
+falls back to a smaller split count when the estimated live workspace does not
+fit the available CUDA allocator budget; an explicit split count that exceeds
+that budget raises `RuntimeError`.
+
+## Sage FP8 forward
+
+Sage FP8 is forward-only and supports blk64 on SM90, SM100/SM103, and SM120,
+plus native blk128 on SM90, SM100/SM103, and SM120. Its public wrapper accepts contiguous
+BF16 Q, K, and V tensors in `BHSD` layout and performs FP8 quantization internally:
+
+```python
+fp8_result = block_sparse_attention_fp8_forward(
+    q,
+    k,
+    v,
+    q2k_block_index,
+    block_sparse_num=4,
+    sparse_block_size=64,
+)
+o_fp8 = fp8_result["o_tensor"]
+```
+
+Q, K, and V must be BF16 MHA tensors in contiguous BHSD layout, have matching
+batch and head counts, and use `D=128`. The wrapper accepts the same sparse
+index metadata used by the regular forward API for the selected block size.
+It lazily loads the quantizer, creates the E4M3 tensors and FP32 scales needed
+by the kernel, and does not expose those implementation details as public
+inputs or outputs.
+
+`sparse_block_size` defaults to 64. On SM120, pass `sparse_block_size=128` with
+`q2k_block_index` shaped `(B, H, ceil(S_q / 128), K_max)` and, when supplied,
+`q2k_block_nums` shaped `(B, H, ceil(S_q / 128))`. Active indices address
+physical 128-token KV blocks, so they must be in `[0, ceil(S_kv / 128))`.
+For `block_sizes`, use `N_kv = ceil(S_kv / 128)` and valid-token counts in
+`[1, 128]` for referenced blocks. The native kernel consumes this metadata
+directly. SM100/SM103 also support this blk128 metadata layout, with the
+additional empty-block and split-KV semantics below.
+
+On SM90, pass `sparse_block_size=128` with indices shaped
+`(B, H, S_q // 128, capacity)` and KV block IDs measured in units of 128 tokens.
+
+The result is a one-key `TupleDict` containing `o_tensor`, a contiguous BF16
+tensor of shape `(B, H, S_q, 128)`. This API does not return LSE and has no
+backward implementation.
+
+V quantization keeps the reciprocal and multiplication in FP32 until the
+final E4M3 conversion, including the internal BHDS and blocked V layouts.
+Q retains the Sage BF16 intermediate-rounding recipe; K uses FP32 centering.
+FP32 rounding near an FP8 midpoint can select an adjacent E4M3 value across
+implementations.
+
+### SM120 per-token Q/K scaling
+
+On SM120 blk128, set `k_quant_block_size=1` to use one FP32 scale for every
+`(batch, head, token)` of **both Q and K**, covering all 128 head features.
+The default `k_quant_block_size=16` preserves the existing recipe. This
+argument controls numerics, not the sparse block size or an autotuning knob.
+
+```python
+out = block_sparse_attention_fp8_forward(
+    q, k, v, q2k_block_index,
+    sparse_block_size=128,
+    k_quant_block_size=1,
+)["o_tensor"]
+```
+
+K is still centered by its FP32 sequence mean before quantization. Its
+per-token descale is `max(amax(abs(K_centered[token, :])), 1e-3) / 448`,
+and the quotient is rounded to E4M3. Q retains its existing BF16 intermediate
+rounding, and V keeps one FP32 scale per `(head, channel)`, reduced over
+**batch and the entire key sequence**. This does not use MXFP8 block-scale
+instructions, Q centering, or a Q-mean/delta correction.
+
+The kernel applies each K descale to its own QK accumulator column before
+the maximum reduction and exponentiation. P uses the unchanged factor of
+256 before E4M3 conversion, with an unrounded FP32 denominator. V descales
+are applied to output channels after PV accumulation. A transposed V storage
+tile of 128 tokens is only a layout choice, **not** a V quantization block.
+
+For blocked V storage, the per-token kernel establishes the maximum over the
+complete 128-key score tile, then converts and consumes P in 32- or 64-key
+chunks. This interleaves probability conversion with PV while retaining the
+original ordered FP32 denominator and K32 MMA accumulation order. The chunk
+width is an internal scheduling choice with a separate compile-cache key;
+it does not change the quantization granularity or normalize each chunk
+independently. The coarse-K and unblocked-V paths retain their existing schedule.
+
+Per-token K requires CuTe DSL >= 4.8.0, SM120, `sparse_block_size=128`, MHA,
+and D=128. Tails, variable sparse counts, empty rows, and partial KV blocks
+follow the existing SM120 contract. Other architectures and blk64 reject
+this option rather than silently falling back to a coarser recipe. Finer
+scales can reduce quantization error, but are not a guarantee of better
+model quality on every input; kernel and quantization-inclusive latency
+should both be measured for the intended workload.
+
+The SM100/SM103 blk128 kernel retains the upstream rounded-probability
+normalization: P uses a factor of 128, and its denominator is accumulated from
+the same rounded FP8 probabilities by the widened PV Tensor Core operation.
+Other FP8 kernels use their existing normalization. Outputs are approximate
+and are not expected to be bitwise equal across block sizes or architectures.
+
+The architecture-specific FP8 contracts are:
+
+- SM90 accepts any positive batch and head counts and requires both sequence
+  lengths to be multiples of the selected `sparse_block_size` (64 or 128).
+  It uses fixed `block_sparse_num` with full KV blocks of that size.
+  Native blk128 shares each K/V tile between two compute warpgroups.
+  Sparse indices may be non-contiguous (including prefix
+  slices, stepped slices, permuted views, and broadcasts); their strides are
+  consumed directly without an index copy. `q2k_block_nums` and `block_sizes`
+  are not supported. It does not use split-KV. V quantization
+  writes sequence-contiguous BHDS storage internally, so the attention kernel
+  directly loads V for Hopper FP8 WGMMA without an in-kernel transpose.
+  Both block sizes accumulate PV directly into FP32 output registers using
+  FP8 WGMMA, accepting its reduced internal accumulation precision instead
+  of promoting each KV tile with a separate FP32 addition.
+- SM100/SM103 blk64 accepts any positive batch and head counts,
+  and requires both sequence lengths to be multiples of 64. It uses fixed
+  `block_sparse_num` with full 64-token KV blocks; `q2k_block_nums` and
+  `block_sizes` are not supported. Split-KV is selected internally, and the
+  public FP8 API does not expose `kv_splits` or `use_clc`.
+- SM100/SM103 native blk128 accepts positive arbitrary Q/KV lengths, including
+  physical tails, with MHA and D=128. Fixed counts may be odd; variable
+  `q2k_block_nums` may be zero, producing zero output. `block_sizes` accepts
+  rank 1, 2, or 3 and values in `[0, 128]`; zero masks a whole block, and the
+  physical final-block length always limits the supplied extent. Inactive
+  index capacity is ignored. Sparse metadata views are materialized as needed.
+  The optional `kv_splits=1..256` partitions the live KV list using FP32 partials
+  and the existing combine kernel; the default is one. Other FP8 paths require
+  the new keyword to remain at its default. `softmax_scale`, when supplied,
+  must be a positive finite host scalar. This implementation is limited to
+  compute capabilities 10.0 and 10.3 and requires CuTe DSL >= 4.6.2.
+- SM120 supports blk64 and blk128, accepts any positive batch and head counts,
+  non-aligned Q/KV sequence tails, fixed or per-query-block counts, and
+  `block_sizes` shaped `(N_kv,)`, `(B, N_kv)`, or `(B, H, N_kv)`. It does not
+  use split-KV.
+
+`block_sparse_attention_fp8_forward` relies on functionality introduced in
+CuTe DSL 4.6.1; the SM90 blk128 path requires 4.6.2. Package-supported
+installations provide CuTe DSL 4.8.0 or newer.
+Its internal Q/K/V quantizer is also implemented in CuTe DSL and is
+loaded lazily, so importing `cudnn` does not eagerly import it.
+
+## Backward
+
+Backward is an explicit API rather than a registered PyTorch autograd
+operation. It recomputes probabilities from the forward output and LSE:
+
+```python
+dout = torch.randn_like(o)
+grads = block_sparse_attention_backward(
+    dout,
+    q,
+    k,
+    v,
+    o,
+    lse,
+    q2k_block_index,
+    block_sparse_num=4,
+    block_sizes=block_sizes,
+    sparse_block_size=64,
+)
+dq, dk, dv = grads
+```
+
+The result keys are `dq_tensor`, `dk_tensor`, and `dv_tensor`. Optional
+preallocated `dq_tensor`, `dk_tensor`, and `dv_tensor` arguments are supported.
+The backward implementation builds a bucketed K-to-Q CSR task layout on the
+GPU. `bucket_size_blocks` is an optional tuning override; leaving it unset uses
+the backend default.
+
+For SM100/SM103 blk128, long-query automatic buckets retain at least one SM
+wave of logical `(batch, head, KV block, query group)` tasks, or the previous
+default's task count when it is smaller. Otherwise, the previous bucket
+default is used. This shape-based guard does not inspect device-side mask
+contents; explicit `bucket_size_blocks` overrides remain authoritative.
+
+For blk64, with contiguous per-row count metadata, at least two KV blocks and at least
+1024 (batch, head, KV block) tasks, backward pairs KV neighborhoods to reuse
+common Q/dO loads and dQ accumulation; smaller problems do not recover the
+per-call pairing cost and use regular tasks.
+Pairing metadata is limited to 64 MiB; fixed counts or unsupported metadata
+layouts use regular tasks. Duplicate sparse edges retain their multiplicity.
+Paired tasks retain FP32 dK/dV accumulation even with a single query bucket;
+regular tasks can use the direct dK/dV epilogue when its alignment requirements hold.
+The initial eight-KV matching is refined within 32-KV windows, with refinement
+skipped above 1024 bitset words. Metadata construction is included in the
+wrapper's work and is rebuilt for each call.
+Backward interleaves its tasks across attention heads only for queries shorter
+than 98,304 tokens, where it was measured to help; longer queries keep the
+head-major task order.
+
+These optimizations keep the public block size at 64 and preserve the existing
+wrapper-owned workspace model. They do not add an allocation-free graph engine.
+Use `benchmark/bsa/benchmark_sm100_blk64.py` for a synthetic complete-API
+comparison; it records the imported source, input hashes and individual CUDA
+Event samples. Numerical tests, sanitizer checks and measurements on each
+target GPU are required before drawing performance conclusions.
+
+Backward defaults to blk64 on SM90 and blk128 on SM100/SM103. Pass the same
+explicit `sparse_block_size` used by forward when selecting the Blackwell blk64
+path. SM100/SM103 blk128 backward accepts one-dimensional `block_sizes`
+(`int32`, shape `(N_kv,)`) and masks each KV block's padded suffix consistently
+with forward. Valid tokens occupy the prefix of each physical block; callers
+zero `dout` for padded queries and discard their outputs. SM110 blk128 backward
+still requires `block_sizes=None`.
+
+## KPage (SM100/SM103 blk128, partially occupied blocks)
+
+`kpage=True` on `block_sparse_attention_forward` and
+`block_sparse_attention_backward` selects a second set of blk128 kernels for
+sparse patterns in which many selected blocks are only partially valid, as
+happens when a 3D video latent is flattened and `block_sizes` marks the rows
+past each block's content. The base kernels load and compute every selected
+block as a full 128-row tile and mask the padding; KPage splits each selected
+K/V block into 16-row pages and gathers only the valid pages, from any blocks,
+into the same 128-row MMA tile during the TMA load. A block with `v` valid
+rows then costs `16 * ceil(v / 16)` rows instead of 128. Query blocks with at
+most 64 valid rows (see `q_block_sizes` below) run on an M64 x N256 kernel,
+the others on M128 x N128. Backward packs K/V pages into owner tiles the same
+way and walks the union of their Q pages with a per-step page-pair mask, so
+`block_sizes` is supported in backward on this path.
+
+```python
+from cudnn.ops import block_sparse_attention_forward, block_sparse_attention_backward, kpage_prepare_layout
+
+# Metadata as for the base path: block_sizes[j] is the number of valid keys of KV block j.
+o, lse = block_sparse_attention_forward(q, k, v, q2k_block_index, block_sparse_num, block_sizes, kpage=True)
+dq, dk, dv = block_sparse_attention_backward(do, q, k, v, o, lse, q2k_block_index, block_sparse_num, block_sizes, kpage=True)
+
+# Reuse one layout across calls; q_block_sizes marks padding on the query side as well.
+layout = kpage_prepare_layout(q2k_block_index, block_sparse_num, block_sizes, q_block_sizes=block_sizes)
+o, lse = block_sparse_attention_forward(q, k, v, q2k_block_index, block_sparse_num, block_sizes, kpage=layout)
+dq, dk, dv = block_sparse_attention_backward(do, q, k, v, o, lse, q2k_block_index, block_sparse_num, block_sizes, kpage=layout)
+```
+
+`kpage=True` computes the same function as the base path with the same
+arguments (`block_sizes` masks keys, every query row is valid) and builds
+the page layout on the call. `kpage_prepare_layout` builds a `KPageLayout`
+once from the metadata so repeated calls with the same sparse pattern (every
+layer of a diffusion step, every training step with a fixed packing) skip the
+metadata kernels. The layout depends on the metadata only, never on `q`, `k`,
+or `v`. Backward tables are built on the first backward call with that layout.
+
+`q_block_sizes` (int32, one entry per query block) is specific to this path:
+query rows at or past `q_block_sizes[i]` in block `i` are padding. They are
+not computed, which is where the M64 x N256 route and part of the speedup on
+video layouts come from, and their rows of `o`, `lse`, and `dq` are written
+as zero. Inputs whose query side carries the same per-block padding as the
+key side pass `q_block_sizes=block_sizes`.
+
+Contract, in addition to the metadata ranges above:
+
+- SM100/SM103, `sparse_block_size=128`, BF16, `head_dim=128`; MHA, GQA, and
+  MQA with metadata per query head (`pack_gqa=None` behaves as `False`,
+  `pack_gqa=True` is not taken); `seqlen_q` and `seqlen_k` independent and
+  arbitrary (rows past a sequence end are padding of its final block, as on
+  the base path); `block_sizes` of shape `(N_kv,)`.
+  BHSD or BSHD tensors (q/k/v/o/do and the gradients) that are compact in
+  their layout. A batch is run as `batch * heads` independent heads, so
+  `block_sizes` is shared across the batch (as on the base SM100 path) and a
+  BSHD batch must be 1. `kv_splits`, `use_clc`, and `bucket_size_blocks`
+  are not taken; a fixed count may be odd.
+- `allow_empty_block_nums` has the base meaning: with `True`, a query block
+  with `q2k_block_nums == 0` gets `O = 0`, `LSE = -inf`, and `dQ = 0`; with
+  `False` (default) such a block is a metadata error. Backward accepts empty
+  blocks as on the base path.
+- Masked key rows (at or past `block_sizes[j]` in block `j`) of `k` and `v`,
+  and padding query rows of `q` and `do` when `q_block_sizes` is given, take
+  no part in the computation and may hold any finite value. Backward writes
+  zeros to the masked rows of `dk` and `dv`. Values on valid rows are exact.
+- `kpage_prepare_layout(validate=True)` (default) checks the metadata on the
+  device with one readback and raises `ValueError` naming the offending entry.
+  The layout build itself reads back three counts; `with_backward=True` also
+  builds the backward tables, which otherwise happens on the first backward
+  call. `seqlen_q` / `seqlen_k` are needed only when a sequence is not a
+  multiple of 128 or when `block_sizes` is omitted and `seqlen_k != seqlen_q`
+  (`kpage=True` takes them from the tensors).
+- A `KPageLayout` remembers the metadata tensors it was built from; passing it
+  together with other metadata, or with tensors of another shape, raises
+  `ValueError`.
+
+The forward output of the KPage path can be fed to the KPage backward or to a
+base backward with `block_sizes=None` when every block is full; the two paths
+compute the same function and differ only in the execution layout.
+
+When to use it: the gain comes from padding (`block_sizes < 128`, and
+`q_block_sizes` for the query side) and grows with the padding fraction
+(1.2-1.3x at 10%, 3.2-3.8x at 59% in `benchmark/bsa`). Without
+padding the page gather costs more than the base kernel's whole-block load,
+so with `block_sizes=None` the base path is faster (measured 0.6x at four
+blocks per row, 0.96x at 128). GQA/MQA run with per-query-head metadata; the
+base path's packed GQA is not available here. BSHD inputs are supported but
+the strided page gathers make the forward slower than on BHSD (measured 1.3x
+on a 16-head layout); prefer BHSD. A `seqlen_k` that is not a multiple of 16
+selects forward kernels whose K/V descriptors carry the row extent instead of
+whole 16-row pages (measured 3-5% slower forward; the backward is
+unaffected), so pad K/V to a multiple of 16 rows when that matters. A call
+carries about 0.1 ms of host work (metadata checks, tensor conversion), which
+only matters for sub-millisecond problems.
+
+### KPage forward on blk64 metadata
+
+On SM100/SM103 `kpage=True` (or a layout built with
+`kpage_prepare_layout(..., sparse_block_size=64)`) also takes
+`sparse_block_size=64` metadata, for the forward only. Every 64-row query
+block is one tile of the M64 x N256 kernel, whose 256-row K/V stage is
+gathered from sixteen 16-row pages, so a selected 64-row block with `v` valid
+rows costs `16 * ceil(v / 16)` rows instead of 64.
+
+```python
+o, lse = block_sparse_attention_forward(q, k, v, q2k_block_index, block_sparse_num, block_sizes, sparse_block_size=64, kpage=True)
+
+layout = kpage_prepare_layout(q2k_block_index, block_sparse_num, block_sizes, q2k_block_nums, sparse_block_size=64)
+o, lse = block_sparse_attention_forward(q, k, v, q2k_block_index, block_sparse_num, block_sizes, q2k_block_nums, sparse_block_size=64, kpage=layout)
+```
+
+The contract is that of the base blk64 forward with these differences:
+
+- BF16, `head_dim=128`, MHA; `seqlen_q` and `seqlen_k` multiples of 64; a
+  BSHD batch must be 1, as above.
+- Every query row is computed, as on the base blk64 path: there is no
+  `q_block_sizes`, and the output rows of query padding are not zeroed.
+- Forward only. `block_sparse_attention_backward(..., kpage=...)` with
+  `sparse_block_size=64` raises; run the base backward on the KPage forward
+  output. A layout is bound to the `sparse_block_size` it was built for.
+
+When to use it: as on blk128, the gain comes from `block_sizes < 64` and
+grows with the padding fraction, and without padding the page gather costs
+more than the base kernel's whole-block load. On random top-k patterns
+(B300, BHSD, layout reused) it measured 1.11-1.36x at 30% padded tokens,
+0.91-1.08x at 10%, and 0.85-0.96x without padding. Building the layout costs
+about 0.3-1 ms per call on those shapes, so reuse a layout from
+`kpage_prepare_layout` whenever the metadata repeats; with `kpage=True` the
+build is paid on every call. Benchmark your own patterns before switching.
+
+## Current support
+
+### Forward
+
+| Architecture | Sparse block | Public input / kernel dtype | QK / V dimensions | Attention |
+| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
+| SM90 | 64 or 128 (explicit) | FP16, BF16 | each of 64, 96, 128 | MHA, GQA, MQA |
+| SM90 | 64 | BF16 / FP8 E4M3 | QK=128, V=128 | MHA |
+| SM90 | 128 (explicit) | BF16 / FP8 E4M3 | QK=128, V=128 | MHA |
+| SM100/SM103 | 128 | FP16, BF16 | QK=V=64, 96, or 128 | MHA, GQA, MQA |
+| SM100/SM103 | 64 (explicit) | BF16 | QK=128, V=128 | MHA |
+| SM100/SM103 | 64 | BF16 / FP8 E4M3 | QK=128, V=128 | MHA |
+| SM100/SM103 | 128 (explicit) | BF16 / FP8 E4M3 | QK=128, V=128 | MHA |
+| SM100/SM103 | 128, `kpage=True` | BF16 | QK=128, V=128 | MHA, GQA, MQA |
+| SM100/SM103 | 64, `kpage=True` | BF16 | QK=128, V=128 | MHA |
+| SM120 | 64 | FP16, BF16 | QK=128, V=128 | MHA, GQA, MQA |
+| SM120 | 128 (explicit) | FP16, BF16 | QK=128, V=128 | MHA, GQA, MQA |
+| SM120 | 64 | BF16 / FP8 E4M3 | QK=128, V=128 | MHA |
+| SM120 | 128 (explicit) | BF16 / FP8 E4M3 | QK=128, V=128 | MHA |
+
+For FP16/BF16, SM90 blk64 requires `S_q` to be a multiple of 64; native blk128 supports
+positive arbitrary Q/KV lengths, including partial final blocks. Its fixed count may be
+any positive value. The SM100/SM103 blk128 fixed count must be even and at
+least two (the KPage path accepts any positive count); SM120 and the explicit
+Blackwell blk64 path accept any positive fixed count. Variable counts use `q2k_block_nums`. `allow_empty_block_nums`
+defaults to `False`; when it is `True`, empty rows (`q2k_block_nums == 0`)
+produce `O = 0` and `LSE = -inf`. SM90 blk64 selects the empty-row handling as a
+compile-time specialization, so the default non-empty configuration keeps its
+branch-free fast path. Its split-KV execution excludes empty rows. Native SM90
+blk128 supports empty rows and empty splits with `kv_splits=1..256`.
+Sage FP8 uses the architecture-specific contracts above. SM100/SM103 native
+blk128 supports empty rows and explicit split-KV; its default remains unsplit.
+
+### Backward
+
+| Architecture | Sparse block | Dtype | Head dimension | Attention |
+| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | --- |
+| SM90 | 64 or 128 (explicit) | BF16 | 128 | MHA |
+| SM100/SM103 | 64 | BF16 | 128 | MHA |
+| SM100/SM103 | 128 | BF16 | 64 or 128 | MHA |
+| SM100/SM103 | 128, `kpage=True` | BF16 | 128 | MHA, GQA, MQA; `block_sizes` supported |
+
+Backward is not implemented for SM120. It requires equal QK/V dimensions and,
+except on the KPage path, does not currently support GQA/MQA.
+
+SM90 native blk128 requires CuTe DSL >= 4.6.2. Q/K/V, O/dO and gradient
+buffers must have a contiguous head dimension, 16-byte aligned base pointers,
+and row strides divisible by 16 bytes. BHSD/BSHD layouts and aligned noncompact
+rows are addressed directly. Sparse metadata can be strided and remains on the
+GPU; backward makes noncontiguous sparse indices and counts contiguous before
+building CSR, as in blk64. Forward supports `block_sizes` of rank 1, 2, or 3; backward supports ranks
+1 and 2. Both paths predicate sequence tails even without `block_sizes`.
+Forward uses Q128 tiles and shares each KV128 load across two compute
+warpgroups. Backward uses Q64xKV128 CTAs: both compute warpgroups execute all
+five GEMMs, splitting KV rows for QK/dP/dK/dV and head dimensions for dQ.
+Each native Q128/KV128 CSR edge streams two Q64 subtiles without expanding
+the metadata. Backward accumulates gradients with FP32 atomics
+and is not deterministic. Benchmark the explicit path for your shapes; blk64
+remains the default, and native blk128 is not faster for every workload.
+
+## Limitations
+
+The current sparse kernels do not implement causal or local masking, dropout,
+`mask_mod`, `score_mod`, paged KV cache, softcap, or variable-length packed
+sequences. Regular forward/backward inputs must be rank four, use FP16/BF16 as
+allowed above, and have a contiguous last (head-dimension) axis. Sage FP8 uses
+the stricter BF16 BHSD contract described above and quantizes to E4M3
+internally. Regular forward outputs are contiguous in the requested BHSD or
+BSHD layout, including split-KV execution; FP8 output is contiguous BF16 BHSD.
+
+Compilation is lazy. The first call for a new static configuration JIT-compiles
+the relevant kernel; subsequent calls reuse an in-process cache.
+
+The Torch public surface consists of allocating function wrappers under
+`cudnn.ops`, also available under `cudnn` and `cudnn.BSA`; there is no separate `APIBase` class or explicit `compile()`
+lifecycle for BSA.
+
+Correctness tests and FP32 references are under
+`test/python/block_sparse_attention/cutedsl`.
+
+## SM100/SM103 FP8 blk128 source
+
+The native producer and its private transfer/epilogue helpers are adapted from
+[NVIDIA-JerryChen/Block-Sparse-Attention, f953680](https://github.com/NVIDIA-JerryChen/Block-Sparse-Attention/tree/f953680ff93a2ef2321ad7dc4291451eea4a9c3c/csrc/fwd/sm100_blk128):
+`bsa_fwd_sm100_fp8_fused_pv.py` and `bsa_fwd_sm100_fp8.py` map to the same
+filenames under `python/cudnn/block_sparse_attention/csrc/fwd/sm100_blk128/`.
+The 16-token TMEM row-max helper is incorporated into the private blk128 helper
+module. The integration uses cuDNN's existing quantizer, allocating Torch API,
+device-specific JIT cache, current-stream execution, and split combine.
+Standalone upstream package entry points and native AOT deployment are not
+part of this API.

+## Experimental JAX support
+
+`cudnn.ops.block_sparse_attention_forward_jax` and
+`cudnn.ops.block_sparse_attention_backward_jax` provide explicit forward/backward;
+`cudnn.jax.block_sparse_attention` adds first-order reverse-mode differentiation.
+All three accept JAX arrays, eagerly or under `jax.jit`, and require no PyTorch.
+`cudnn.jax.block_sparse_attention_forward` and `cudnn.jax.block_sparse_attention_backward`
+have been removed; use the `cudnn.ops` names.
+
+The JAX implementation reuses the SM100 blk128 forward, bucketed CSR, backward preprocess,
+backward, and gradient conversion kernels. Install `jax[cuda13]` alongside the
+frontend (CuTeDSL >=4.7, JAX >=0.9.1). The runtime imports no PyTorch; torch parity tests are separate.
+
+The JAX signatures omit Torch-specific launch options and caller-provided
+output buffers. XLA owns the outputs and workspaces.
+
+### Initial contract
+
+| Property | Supported |
+| --- | --- |
+| Device | All arrays on one CUDA GPU of exactly compute capability 10.0 (SM100); other GPUs may be visible. Single process |
+| Data | BF16 Q/K/V/O/dO/dQ/dK/dV; FP32 LSE and accumulation |
+| Dimensions | MHA with equal head counts, D=64 or 128; positive sequence lengths divisible by 128 |
+| Layout | Compact BHSD or BSHD, independently specialized |
+| Sparsity | 128-token blocks, int32 indices `[B,H,Sq/128,C]`, no `block_sizes` |
+| Counts | Fixed even `block_sparse_num` in `[2,C]`, or runtime int32 `q2k_block_nums[B,H,Sq/128]` |
+| Differentiation | First-order reverse-mode Q/K/V gradients through `block_sparse_attention` |
+
+Variable counts must be in `[1,C]`, or `[0,C]` with
+`allow_empty_block_nums=True`. Only each row's active prefix is read. Active
+indices must be unique and in `[0,Sk/128)`. An empty row returns zero output,
+negative-infinity LSE, and zero query gradient. Unselected K/V receive zero
+contributions. Metadata **values are the caller's responsibility**: the runtime
+validates shapes, dtypes, and static options, without copying metadata to the
+host or synchronizing to inspect it. Invalid values are outside the contract.
+
+SM103/SM110/SM120, blk64, FP16/FP8, GQA, different V dimensions, partial blocks,
+variable sequence lengths, causal masks, dropout, sharding, `vmap`, JVP, and
+higher derivatives are unsupported. KDA is outside this change. Static options
+(including scale and fixed count) specialize compilation; sparse arrays remain
+runtime operands. Do not mutate saved forward inputs or metadata before backward.
+
+### Usage
+
+```python
+import jax
+import jax.numpy as jnp
+from functools import partial
+from cudnn.jax import block_sparse_attention as attention
+from cudnn.ops import (
+    block_sparse_attention_forward_jax as forward,
+    block_sparse_attention_backward_jax as backward,
+)
+
+q = jnp.ones((1, 2, 256, 64), dtype=jnp.bfloat16)
+k = jnp.ones((1, 2, 512, 64), dtype=jnp.bfloat16)
+v = jnp.ones_like(k)
+indices = jnp.broadcast_to(jnp.array([0, 2], jnp.int32), (1, 2, 2, 2))
+
+o, lse = forward(q, k, v, indices, 2)  # eager; asynchronous GPU execution
+run = jax.jit(partial(forward, block_sparse_num=2))
+result = run(q, k, v, indices)
+o, lse = result["o_tensor"], result["lse_tensor"]
+
+dq, dk, dv = backward(jnp.ones_like(o), q, k, v, o, lse, indices, 2)
+
+def loss(q, k, v, indices):
+    return attention(q, k, v, indices, 2).astype(jnp.float32).sum()
+
+grad = jax.jit(jax.grad(loss, argnums=(0, 1, 2)))
+dq, dk, dv = grad(q, k, v, indices)
+dq.block_until_ready()  # needed for host timing, not between GPU operations
+```
+
+Explicit forward returns a JAX pytree with `o_tensor`, `lse_tensor`; backward returns `dq_tensor`,
+`dk_tensor`, `dv_tensor`. Both support tuple unpacking and dictionary access. Explicit helpers
+do not register autodiff rules; use `attention` for `jax.grad`. LSE and metadata
+are not differentiable public outputs. Backward must receive the exact matching
+forward Q/K/V/O/LSE, sparse pattern, scale, layout, and empty-row option.
+
+### Execution and ownership
+
+Every launch receives XLA's CUDA stream. Forward is one custom call; backward
+composes CSR construction, preprocessing, attention backward, and gradient
+conversion inside one custom call. XLA owns all outputs and workspaces. CSR
+counts and multi-bucket dK/dV accumulators are initialized for each invocation;
+preprocessing clears dQ accumulation. No mutable global scratch or public input
+buffer is donated. Atomic accumulation does not promise bitwise determinism.
+
+`TensorSpec.mode` presents compact BHSD/BSHD memory in the order expected by each
+kernel. It does not rewrite DLPack capsules or insert a Python transpose. XLA may
+still insert layout conversions when surrounding operations use incompatible
+physical layouts; this is not a universal zero-copy guarantee.
+

+# DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA)
+
+**This is an experimental API and subject to change.**
+
+Torch-facing calls accept the ordinary default stream or a concrete
+`torch.cuda.Stream` / raw stream handle. The special `CUstream(2)` per-thread
+default sentinel is rejected by Torch interop: it cannot safely represent an
+allocator stream identity across host threads. Use a concrete stream instead.
+
+## Overview
+
+The DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA) module integrates a set of CuTe-DSL
+kernels that support the sparse-attention path used by DeepSeek-style models.
+Most kernels target Hopper (SM90) and Blackwell (SM100+) GPUs. Sparse-attention
+forward and the combined compressed-logits + Top-K path are SM100-only;
+sparse-attention forward is limited to the mapped SM100-family capabilities
+10.0, 10.3, and 10.7. Dense Indexer Forward and standalone Indexer Top-K
+support both architectures. The kernels are delivered as Python classes /
+wrappers that follow the same `APIBase` pattern as other cuDNN Frontend
+operations.
+
+**Scope:** this module ships CuTe-DSL kernels for sparse-attention forward and
+backward, indexer scores/top-K, sparse/dense score recompute, and sparse/dense
+indexer backward. Sparse forward covers regular H64 and small-top-k Prefill
+H128; it does not include the H128 decode/split-KV mode.
+
+The module packages the following operations:
+
+1. **Sparse Attention Forward** – sparse Prefill MQA for the supported SM100
+   H64/H128 shapes.
+2. **Sparse Attention Backward** – DSA backward for flat MQA tensors on
+   SM90/SM100.
+3. **Indexer Forward** – CuTe-DSL score kernel (Q @ K^T, ReLU, head reduce,
+   ratio causal mask) that materializes dense scores.
+4. **Combined Indexer Forward + Top-K** – SM100 compact score generation,
+   Top-K selection, and optional Top-K softmax in one public API call.
+5. **Indexer Top-K** – SM90+ CuTe-DSL radix top-K kernel with per-row
+   ``seq_lens``.
+6. **Sparse Indexer / Attention Score Recompute** – sparse (top-K) recompute
+   of indexer and attention scores for training loss.
+7. **Dense Indexer / Attention Score Recompute** – dense (full-KV) analogues
+   of the above.
+8. **Indexer Backward** – three-stage pipeline (score-grad, three
+   GEMMs, dtype cast) for sparse top-K score tensors.
+9. **Dense Indexer Backward** – full-KV counterpart of Indexer Backward.
+
+### Architecture
+
+```text
+Q, K, W ──┬─► IndexerForward ──► scores ──► IndexerTopK ──► topk_idxs
+          └─► IndexerForwardTopK ──► topk_idxs, logits, predict
+                                                             │
+                                                             v
+                              SparseAttentionForward ──► out, lse
+                                                             │
+                                                      dout ──┤
+                                                             v
+                                               SparseAttentionBackward
+                                                             │
+                                                             v
+                                                    dq, dkv, d_sink
+
+Training-score loss path:
+   attn_score, index_score ──► IndexerBackward ──► d_index_q, d_weights, d_index_k
+   (SparseIndexer/AttnScoreRecompute and DenseIndexer/AttnScoreRecompute
+   produce these score tensors; DenseIndexerBackward consumes dense raw scores.)
+```
+
+---
+
+## Installation
+
+```bash
+pip install nvidia-cudnn-frontend
+```
+
+---
+
+## API Usage
+
+### DSA Namespace
+
+```python
+from cudnn import DSA
+
+DSA.SparseAttentionBackward
+DSA.sparse_attention_backward_wrapper
+
+DSA.SparseAttentionForward
+DSA.sparse_attention_forward_wrapper
+
+DSA.IndexerForward
+DSA.indexer_forward_wrapper
+DSA.indexer_forward_top_k_wrapper
+DSA.compress_topk_cand_buffer_size
+DSA.compress_topk_cand_buffer_size_thd
+
+DSA.IndexerTopK
+DSA.indexer_top_k_wrapper
+DSA.local_to_global_wrapper
+DSA.compactify_wrapper
+
+DSA.SparseIndexerScoreRecompute
+DSA.sparse_indexer_score_recompute_wrapper
+
+DSA.SparseAttnScoreRecompute
+DSA.sparse_attn_score_recompute_wrapper
+
+DSA.DenseIndexerScoreRecompute
+DSA.dense_indexer_score_recompute_wrapper
+
+DSA.DenseAttnScoreRecompute
+DSA.dense_attn_score_recompute_wrapper
+
+DSA.IndexerBackward
+DSA.indexer_backward_wrapper
+
+DSA.DenseIndexerBackward
+DSA.dense_indexer_backward_wrapper
+```
+
+---
+
+## Components
+
+### 1. Sparse Attention Forward
+
+Sparse Prefill forward for flat MQA tensors. For query row `t`, head `h`, and
+valid top-k slot `j`, the score is
+`softmax_scale * dot(q[t,h,:], kv[topk_idxs[t,j],:])`. Invalid and OOB indices
+have score `-inf`; duplicate indices remain distinct softmax slots. The
+attention sink participates only in the output denominator, not in any stats.
+
+- **Inputs**
+  - `q`: `(total_S_q, H, D_qk)` FP16 or BF16
+  - `kv`: `(total_S_kv, D_qk)`, with the same dtype as `q` (K = V latent; MQA)
+  - `topk_idxs`: `(total_S_q, K)` INT32 global token ids; K may be any
+    nonnegative value and is padded internally to a multiple of 64
+  - `attn_sink` (optional): `(H,)` FP32
+  - `topk_length` (optional): `(total_S_q,)` INT32, clamped to `[0, K]`
+  - `softmax_scale` (optional runtime float): defaults to `1 / sqrt(D_qk)`
+  - `indexer_topk`: compile-time prefix length
+- **Outputs** — stable `TupleDict` keys:
+  - `out`: `(total_S_q, H, 512)`, with the same dtype as `q`
+  - `max_logits`: `(total_S_q, H)` FP32
+  - `lse`: `(total_S_q, H)` FP32, KV-only and excluding the sink
+  - `lse_indexer`: `(total_S_q, H)` FP32, or `None` for `indexer_topk=0`
+- **Variants**
+  - H64: `D_qk in {512, 576}`, `indexer_topk in {0, 512, 1024, 2048}`
+  - H128 small-top-k Prefill: `D_qk=512`,
+    `indexer_topk in {0, 512, 1024}`
+- **Indexer prefix constraint** — `indexer_topk <= K`; when `topk_length` is
+  supplied and indexer LSE is enabled, every row must have
+  `topk_length >= indexer_topk`, matching the tile-boundary snapshot
+  contract.
+- **Empty rows** — `out=0`, `max_logits=-inf`, `lse=+inf`; an enabled
+  `lse_indexer` is also `+inf`.
+- **Compilation lifecycle** — `SparseAttentionForward.compile()` validates
+  and primes the API object, while the concrete CuTe kernel is JIT-compiled
+  on its first `execute()`/wrapper call because padding and live DLPack
+  layouts are runtime properties.
+- **Layout and stream** — non-contiguous or under-aligned Q/KV inputs are
+  materialized on the selected stream. An explicit `stream` must be a
+  `cuda.bindings.driver.CUstream` belonging to `q.device`.
+
+For `D_qk=576`, QK uses all 576 dimensions while V/output uses only the first
+512 KV dimensions. `attn_sink=None` is equivalent to an all-`-inf` sink.
+
+```python
+import math
+
+result = DSA.sparse_attention_forward_wrapper(
+    q,
+    kv,
+    topk_idxs,
+    attn_sink=attn_sink,
+    topk_length=topk_length,
+    softmax_scale=1.0 / math.sqrt(q.shape[-1]),
+    indexer_topk=512,
+)
+out = result["out"]
+max_logits = result["max_logits"]
+lse = result["lse"]
+lse_indexer = result["lse_indexer"]
+```
+
+### 2. Sparse Attention Backward
+
+Backward pass for DeepSeek Sparse Attention. Expects the forward wrapper's
+`out` and KV-only `lse` (or equivalent tensors).
+
+- **Inputs**
+  - `q`: `(total_S_q, H, D)` BF16/FP16
+  - `kv`: `(total_S_kv, D)` (K = V; MQA)
+  - `out`, `dout`: `(total_S_q, H, D_v)`
+  - `lse`: `(total_S_q, H)` FP32
+  - `attn_sink`: `(H,)` FP32
+  - `topk_idxs`: `(total_S_q, topk_max)` INT32 (global)
+  - `topk_length` (optional): `(total_S_q,)` INT32 — per-query valid count.
+    The H128 two-CTA backends (D512 and D576) clamp it to `[0, topk_max]`
+    and ignore every slot after that prefix, including valid indices pointing
+    to nonfinite KV rows; the other backends expect `topk_length <= topk_max`.
+    Omitting this tensor uses all `topk_max` slots.
+
+On Blackwell SM100/SM103, the public backward entry point automatically selects
+the tuned kernel from the device, dtype, and tensor shape. On SM100 (10, 0) and
+SM103 (10, 3) devices, BF16 H128 with `head_dim = head_dim_v = 512` and
+`topk_max ∈ {128, 512, 1024, 1152, 2048}` uses the two-CTA specialization.
+Contiguous BF16 H128 with `head_dim = 576`, `head_dim_v = 512`, and the same
+`topk_max` set uses the H128/D576 two-CTA specialization. H16 with
+`head_dim=576` uses the dedicated M128 sparse-row pipeline. FP16, other head
+counts and dimensions, and every other `topk_max` retain the existing
+generic/H16/H32 selection. Other compute capabilities, including SM107, do not
+select the two-CTA paths. No backend or tile-size argument is required. SM90
+continues to use its Hopper-specific implementation. Every input must be
+contiguous on every route: `check_support()` declines a strided tensor with
+`NotImplementedError` naming it and its strides, and `execute()` rejects one
+with `ValueError`; the plan never repacks an input.
+
+The SM100 H16/H32/H96 D576 specializations compile the physical row stride of
+`topk_idxs` from `topk_max`, while the query count and per-query `topk_length`
+remain dynamic. H64 and the generic/H128 D512 paths retain their existing
+layout; H128 D576 already uses a static `topk_max` stride.
+
+For contiguous BF16 H16/H32 D576 inputs, `q_cluster_mode="adaptive_pair"`
+enables adjacent-query KV sharing. A device-side transform partitions each
+pair into one tile-aligned intersection and two unique segments, then evaluates
+the intersection with twice the head count. Its bounded hash storage scales
+with `topk_max` rather than `total_S_kv`; invalid, duplicate, low-overlap, and
+an odd final query retain the ordinary per-query work. The mode is opt-in,
+non-deterministic, CUDA Graph compatible, and supports `topk_max <= 2048`.
+It is intended for high-overlap workloads; the device-side partition still
+runs when a pair falls back to ordinary work. H16 `topk_max <= 256` and H32
+`topk_max <= 128` accept the mode but compile the ordinary backend directly.
+
+With the default `deterministic=False`, the H128 specialization keeps the five tensor-core products in one
+two-CTA main kernel. It publishes FP32 O-dot-dO and folded-LSE statistics to the
+caller-provided scratch workspace, converts the FP32 dKV workspace to the public BF16
+output, and completes dSink with a separate FP32 reduction kernel. The helper
+launches do not change the two-CTA topology of the core computation.
+
+The H128/D576 specialization applies the same two-CTA topology to the MLA
+layout (`head_dim = 576`, `head_dim_v = 512`). Its compiled sequence
+with `deterministic=False` initializes the FP32 dKV workspace and the dSink output on the launch stream,
+accumulates dKV in that workspace, and converts it to the public BF16 output
+with a helper kernel. With the default `deterministic=False`, short query
+batches split each query's top-k range across otherwise idle two-SM clusters;
+the split count is fixed when the plan is compiled.
+
+On SM100/SM103, `deterministic=True` retains the two-CTA Tensor Core kernels
+for the supported BF16 H128/D512 and H128/D576 envelopes above. Queries run in
+same-stream waves of at most 74 query tokens, with one two-CTA pair per query.
+Private FP32 accumulator slots and ordered duplicate-index writers give each
+update a fixed accumulation order. Stream ordering serializes slot reuse
+between waves, and fixed-order reductions produce `dKV` and `d_sink`. Both
+specializations keep the public workspace capacity of 128 FP32 dKV planes.
+
+Other deterministic envelopes with H16/H32/H64/H96/H128 use the bounded-wave
+M64 implementation. Ordinary extents select 32 dKV shards for
+`total_S_q <= 128`, 64 for `129..256`, and 128 for larger query batches.
+Queries run in same-stream waves with one CTA per shard; CTA lane `i` is the
+sole writer of FP32 dKV shard `i` in each wave. H16/H32 use a masked M64 head
+tile. H96/H128 split each query wave into ordered M64 head-block launches,
+preserving single-writer ownership without multiplying the number of shards.
+Kernel launch ordering serializes both head blocks and shard reuse across
+waves. The 32-shard specialization converts with one fixed-order reduction;
+the 64- and 128-shard specializations first fold groups of eight and then
+combine those groups in fixed order.
+
+If the selected bounded-wave layout would exceed 16 GiB, the generic M64 plan
+keeps each query wave at 128 CTAs and assigns one FP32 dKV plane to each
+cluster. Queries below 8192 rows prefer sixteen eight-CTA clusters; larger
+queries prefer thirty-two four-CTA clusters for additional reducer parallelism.
+If that preferred layout's complete FP32-plane and packed-mask allocation would
+exceed 32 GiB, the plan selects an eight-plane, sixteen-CTA memory-first relay.
+The long-query policy deliberately skips cluster-8: GB200 sweeps at 393K, 512K,
+and 768K KV found it slower than cluster-16 while retaining twice as many FP32
+planes. A setup kernel builds packed 16-bit, 8-bit, or 4-bit rank masks for every
+`(query wave, head block, KV row)`. Reducer threads wait only for lower cluster
+ranks that actually update the same KV row, then publish that row with
+GPU-scope release/acquire ordering. The participating reducer-thread CTA
+barrier carries the release/acquire causality, so no additional GPU-wide fence
+is needed. Rank zero skips the predecessor handoff, the last rank skips the
+successor publication, and the final release needs no second rendezvous.
+Disjoint sparse rows continue in parallel; the fixed rank order handles both
+low- and high-overlap top-k rows without a global semaphore dependency on
+non-resident CTAs. The selected 8, 16, or 32 planes are combined directly in
+the fixed-order conversion kernel, without an intermediate FP32 prefold.
+Duplicate top-k indices within one query row remain outside the deterministic
+contract, as in the bounded-wave path. This condition is not checked at
+runtime; callers that require bitwise repeatability must provide unique valid
+indices within each query's active top-k prefix.
+
+For the ordinary policy, additional dKV workspace is
+`selected_shards * K8 * D8 * sizeof(float)`, where
+`K8 = round_up(total_S_kv, 8)` and `D8 = round_up(D, 8)`. The cluster relay
+uses `relay_planes * (K8 + mask_rows) * D8 * sizeof(float)`, where
+`relay_planes` is 8, 16, or 32, `relay_width` is 16, 8, or 4, and
+`mask_rows = ceil(ceil(total_S_q / 128) * ceil(H / 64) *
+(K8 / (32 / relay_width)) / D8)`.
+One CTA per head reduces `d_sink`. Use `scratch_workspace_bytes()` as the
+authoritative full scratch size; a larger reusable workspace remains valid.
+Treat this as a reproducibility requirement rather than a performance-tuning
+knob: keep the default `False` when bitwise run-to-run stability is not needed.
+
