+    """An O-shaped half gate; row 0 (the all-dead row of the multi-row partial patterns) holds NaN, which must never reach the output."""
+    gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
+    gate = (torch.randn(b, sq, h, d, generator=gen) * 3.0).to(dtype)
+    if sq > 1:
+        gate[:, 0] = torch.nan
+    return gate.cuda()
+
+
+_FORMS = ("auto", "on", "off", "walk")
+"""Every form the entry can take: AUTO = the adapters' entry, ON / OFF the forced kernels, WALK the lean group walk (the cc 10.7 adapter's form
+on a lean-grid-overflow plan; the entry obeys its selector whatever the grid)."""
+
+
+_ROUNDINGS = ("single", "staged")
+"""The fused store's two rounding conventions (``heuristics.COMBINE_OUT_ROUNDINGS``): one rounding of the fp32 gated value, and a serving stack's
+gate-and-quantize order (bf16 only)."""
+
+# Whether the staged bytes are asserted BITWISE the torch model of the stack's convention (``_staged_twin``), or only within one e4m3 code with
+# the histogram printed.  The two could part only through the exp lowering: the DSL's precise ``exp`` ends in ``ex2.approx.ftz`` scaled by
+# ``2^j`` through an fma whose ``+ 1`` (the sigmoid's denominator) the compiler contracts into it, where torch's CUDA ``exp`` rounds its result
+# before the add -- but the scaling by a power of two is exact, so the fma rounds ``e + 1`` exactly as the separate add does, and the two libms
+# are the same algorithm.  MEASURED bitwise on a cc 10.0 part on every cell of this module (74 histograms, 0 elements one code off); the bound
+# is never widened past one code.
+STAGED_TWIN_BITWISE = True
+
+
+def _entries(comb, *, fused, tag, use_pdl=False, forms=_FORMS, rounding="single"):
+    """The ``forms`` of the fused e4m3 entry (``rounding``: its convention) or of its unfused twin, the gated half entry of the same form
+    (``dtype_o`` = the gate's half dtype; no convention)."""
+    codes = {"auto": comb.DECODE_GRID_AUTO, "on": comb.DECODE_GRID_ON, "off": comb.DECODE_GRID_OFF, "walk": comb.DECODE_GRID_LEAN_WALK}
+    kw = dict(dtype_partial="f32", has_lse=True, gate=True, dtype_gate=tag, use_pdl=use_pdl)
+    kw.update(dict(dtype_o="e4m3", gate_e4m3=True, out_rounding=rounding) if fused else dict(dtype_o=tag))
+    return {name: positional_entry(comb.compile_ptr(**kw, decode_grid=codes[name])) for name in forms}
+
+
+def _plain_entries(comb, forms=_FORMS):
+    """The ``forms`` of the UNGATED bf16 half entry: its store is ``bf16(acc * inv_den)``, the value the staged convention rounds first (the bf16
+    attention output a serving stack's gate-and-quantize kernel reads)."""
+    codes = {"auto": comb.DECODE_GRID_AUTO, "on": comb.DECODE_GRID_ON, "off": comb.DECODE_GRID_OFF, "walk": comb.DECODE_GRID_LEAN_WALK}
+    return {name: positional_entry(comb.compile_ptr(dtype_o="bf16", dtype_partial="f32", has_lse=True, decode_grid=codes[name])) for name in forms}
+
+
+def _launch(fn, op, lp, b, h, sq, d, splits, gate, *, scale=None, out_dtype=torch.bfloat16, o=None):
+    """One launch: the fused entry when ``scale`` is given (the e4m3 output pre-filled with the e4m3 MAX as a canary), else the gated half
+    entry (the half output pre-filled with -31) -- or, with ``gate`` None, the ungated half entry; the final LSE pre-filled with -31."""
+    if o is None:
+        o = torch.full((b, sq, h, d), E4M3_MAX if scale is not None else -31.0, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn if scale is not None else out_dtype)
+    lse = torch.full((b, h, sq), -31.0, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32)
+    extra = ((gate.data_ptr(), gate.stride()) if gate is not None else ()) + ((scale.data_ptr(),) if scale is not None else ())
+    fn(
+        op.data_ptr(),
+        lp.data_ptr(),
+        o.data_ptr(),
+        lse.data_ptr(),
+        (b, h, sq, d),
+        splits,
+        o.stride(),
+        lse.stride(),
+        *extra,
+        torch.cuda.current_stream().cuda_stream,
+    )
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    return o, lse
+
+
+def _ulp_e4m3(x):
+    """The e4m3 spacing at |x| (fp32 tensor): ``2^(floor(log2 |x|) - 3)`` for a normal value (|x| >= 2^-6), the subnormal spacing 2^-9 below."""
+    mag = x.abs().clamp_min(2.0**-6)
+    return torch.exp2(torch.floor(torch.log2(mag)) - 3.0)
+
+
+def _ulp_distance(a, b):
+    """|a - b| in e4m3 ulps AT THE LARGER MAGNITUDE (a one-ulp claim names its unit and its twin); both fp32 tensors."""
+    a, b = a.float(), b.float()
+    return (a - b).abs() / _ulp_e4m3(torch.maximum(a.abs(), b.abs()))
+
+
+def _histogram(dist):
+    """Counts of exact / one-ulp / more-than-one-ulp differences (the number the report quotes, never a bitwise claim)."""
+    exact = int((dist == 0).sum())
+    one = int(((dist > 0) & (dist <= 1.0 + 1e-6)).sum())
+    more = int((dist > 1.0 + 1e-6).sum())
+    return dict(exact=exact, one_ulp=one, more=more, max_ulp=float(dist.max()) if dist.numel() else 0.0)
+
+
+def _unfused_twin(o_half, scale):
+    """The production path the fused entry replaces: the gated half output cast in torch at the same ``inv`` (fp32 ``1 / scale``, RN)."""
+    inv = torch.ones((), dtype=torch.float32, device=o_half.device) / scale.float().reshape(())
+    return (o_half.float() * inv).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+
+
+def _gate_quant_model(ref_o, gate, scale, half_dtype):
+    """The serving stacks' gate-and-quantize convention on the float64 merged reference: the attention output as a half tensor (the attention kernel's
+    own output), the gated value rounded to half, then ``* inv`` in fp32 and the e4m3 cast (an exact sigmoid; two half roundings)."""
+    inv = torch.ones((), dtype=torch.float32) / scale.float().cpu().reshape(())
+    attn = ref_o.float().to(half_dtype).float()
+    g = gate.float().cpu()
+    gated = (attn * torch.sigmoid(g)).to(half_dtype).float()
+    return (gated * inv).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+
+
+def _staged_twin(attn_bf16, gate, scale):
+    """The torch model of the STAGED convention, on the device, on the bf16 attention output ``attn_bf16`` (the ungated half entry's store of the
+    same form = ``bf16(acc * inv_den)``, the value the staged arm rounds first): ``e4m3(rn, satfinite)(bf16(a / (1 + exp(-g))) * div.rn(1, s))`` --
+    the sigmoid as a DIVISION (never ``a * sigmoid(g)``: a different rounding), torch's CUDA ``exp``, the bf16 rounding of the quotient, the fp32
+    multiply by the RN inverse, and torch's e4m3 cast after a clamp to +-448 (torch reads NaN from 480 up where ``cvt.rn.satfinite`` saturates;
+    the clamp makes the two one function on every finite value).  Differs from the kernel only where the exp lowerings part (``STAGED_TWIN_BITWISE``)."""
+    inv = torch.ones((), dtype=torch.float32, device=attn_bf16.device) / scale.float().reshape(())
+    a, g = attn_bf16.float(), gate.float()
+    v = (a / (1.0 + torch.exp(-g))).to(torch.bfloat16).float()
+    return (v * inv).clamp(-E4M3_MAX, E4M3_MAX).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+
+
+def _single_model(attn_bf16, gate, scale):
+    """The torch model of the SINGLE convention on a bf16-valued merged value: ``e4m3(a * sigmoid(g) * inv)``, one rounding of the fp32 gated
+    value -- within one ulp of the kernel's tanh form (an approximate tanh), never bitwise; the exact-merge cell's second reference."""
+    inv = torch.ones((), dtype=torch.float32, device=attn_bf16.device) / scale.float().reshape(())
+    return (attn_bf16.float() * torch.sigmoid(gate.float()) * inv).clamp(-E4M3_MAX, E4M3_MAX).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+
+
+def _check_staged_twin(hist, what):
+    """The staged-vs-model verdict: within one code always (``_check_fused`` asserted it); bitwise when the record says the lowerings agree."""
+    if STAGED_TWIN_BITWISE:
+        assert hist["one_ulp"] == 0, f"{what}: {hist['one_ulp']} elements one code off the stack-convention model (expected bitwise): {hist}"
+
+
+def _live_rows(ref_lse):
+    """A [B, S_q, H] live mask from the float64 reference LSE ([B, H, S_q])."""
+    return torch.isfinite(ref_lse).permute(0, 2, 1)
+
+
+def _check_fused(fused, twin, lse_fused, lse_twin, ref_lse, *, what, max_ulp=1.0):
+    """The fused bytes against a twin's bytes on the LIVE rows within ``max_ulp`` (unit: the e4m3 ulp at the larger magnitude), no NaN bytes,
+    dead rows exactly 0 on the fused output, the LSE bitwise; returns the histogram."""
+    live = _live_rows(ref_lse)
+    f, t = fused.cpu().float(), twin.cpu().float()
+    assert not torch.isnan(f).any(), f"{what}: a NaN byte in the fused output"
+    dead = ~live
+    if dead.any():
+        assert torch.count_nonzero(f[dead.unsqueeze(-1).expand_as(f)]).item() == 0, f"{what}: a dead row is not exactly 0"
+    lv = live.unsqueeze(-1).expand_as(f)
+    dist = _ulp_distance(f[lv], t[lv])
+    hist = _histogram(dist)
+    assert hist["more"] == 0, f"{what}: {hist['more']} elements differ by more than {max_ulp} e4m3 ulp (max {hist['max_ulp']:.3f}): {hist}"
+    if lse_twin is not None:
+        assert torch.equal(lse_fused, lse_twin), f"{what}: the LSE must be bitwise the half entry's (it never sees the gate or the scale)"
+    return hist
+

+def test_fused_keeps_the_fp32_magnitude_where_the_f16_twin_underflows_before_the_scale(_m):
+    """The BOUNDARY of the one-ulp twin claim, recorded as intended: B = H = S_q = 1, D 128, four identical fp32 partials of 1e-8 under a
+    zero partial LSE (the merged value 1e-8, the final LSE log 4), a zero gate (sigmoid 1/2: the fp32 gated value 5e-9) and the positive
+    normal scale 1e-10 (``inv`` 1e10: the scaled value is fp32 50, an e4m3 tie that rounds to even).  Every form of the fused entry stores
+    48 -- the fp32 magnitude, rounded once -- with the LSE bitwise the half entry's.  The f16 twin underflows BEFORE the scale: 5e-9 is
+    below 2^-25, half of f16's smallest subnormal, so the gated f16 entry stores 0 and its cast reads 0 -- 12 e4m3 ulp at the larger
+    magnitude; the twin is not a general bound.  bf16 does not underflow there (its smallest normal is 2^-126): the gated bf16 entry stores
+    bf16(5e-9) = 5.0059e-9 and its cast reads 52, within the one ulp the claim names.  The single rounding is the contract; the twin bounds
+    it only where the half dtype keeps the magnitude."""
+    from cudnn.sdpa.fwd.kernels.sm100 import split_combine as comb
+
+    b, h, sq, d, splits = 1, 1, 1, 128, 4
+    op = torch.full((splits * b, sq, h, d), 1e-8, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32)
+    lp = torch.zeros((splits * b, h, sq), device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32)
+    ref_lse = torch.full((b, h, sq), math.log(splits), dtype=torch.float64)  # every row live
+    scale = torch.tensor([1e-10], dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda")
+    for dtype, tag, twin_want, ulp_want in ((torch.float16, "f16", 0.0, 12.0), (torch.bfloat16, "bf16", 52.0, 1.0)):
+        gate = torch.zeros((b, sq, h, d), device="cuda", dtype=dtype)
+        fused_fns = _entries(comb, fused=True, tag=tag)
+        twin_fns = _entries(comb, fused=False, tag=tag)
+        for name in _FORMS:
+            o1, l1 = _launch(fused_fns[name], op, lp, b, h, sq, d, splits, gate, scale=scale)
+            ot, lt = _launch(twin_fns[name], op, lp, b, h, sq, d, splits, gate, out_dtype=dtype)
+            f, half_o, twin = o1.cpu().float(), ot.cpu().float(), _unfused_twin(ot, scale).cpu().float()
+            dist = _ulp_distance(f, twin)
+            print(
+                f"\nboundary {tag} {name}: fused {f.unique().tolist()} half entry {half_o.unique().tolist()} twin {twin.unique().tolist()} "
+                f"ulp {dist.unique().tolist()} lse {l1.flatten().tolist()}"
+            )
+            assert torch.all(f == 48.0), f"{tag} {name}: the fused store reads 48 everywhere (fp32 50 -> e4m3 ties to even); got {f.unique().tolist()}"
+            assert torch.equal(l1, lt), f"{tag} {name}: the LSE is bitwise the half entry's"
+            assert torch.allclose(l1.cpu(), torch.full((b, h, sq), math.log(splits)), atol=1e-5), l1  # the final LSE is log 4 (m 0, den 4)
+            assert torch.all(twin == twin_want) and torch.all(dist == ulp_want), (tag, name, twin.unique().tolist(), dist.unique().tolist())
+            if dtype == torch.float16:
+                assert torch.all(half_o == 0.0), f"{name}: the gated f16 entry underflows before the scale"
+            else:
+                assert torch.all(half_o != 0.0), f"{name}: the gated bf16 entry keeps the magnitude"
+                _check_fused(o1, _unfused_twin(ot, scale), l1, lt, ref_lse, what=f"boundary bf16 {name}")  # the claim holds where the twin keeps it
+    # the STAGED convention on the same cell (bf16 only): the merged 1e-8 rounds to bf16 1.0012e-8, halved by the exact sigmoid of the zero gate
+    # and rounded to bf16 5.0059e-9, times 1e10 = 50.06 -> e4m3 52 on every form (the bf16 twin's value: the mode is honoured where the two
+    # conventions part), the LSE bitwise the half entry's
+    gate = torch.zeros((b, sq, h, d), device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    staged_fns = _entries(comb, fused=True, tag="bf16", rounding="staged")
+    twin_fns = _entries(comb, fused=False, tag="bf16")
+    for name in _FORMS:
+        o1, l1 = _launch(staged_fns[name], op, lp, b, h, sq, d, splits, gate, scale=scale)
+        ot, lt = _launch(twin_fns[name], op, lp, b, h, sq, d, splits, gate, out_dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        f = o1.cpu().float()
+        print(f"\nboundary staged bf16 {name}: fused {f.unique().tolist()} lse {l1.flatten().tolist()}")
+        assert torch.all(
+            f == 52.0
+        ), f"staged bf16 {name}: the staged store reads 52 everywhere (bf16(bf16(1e-8) / 2) x 1e10 = 50.06); got {f.unique().tolist()}"
+        assert torch.equal(l1, lt), f"staged bf16 {name}: the LSE is bitwise the half entry's"

+def test_fused_store_saturates_at_the_e4m3_range_and_never_writes_nan(rounding):
+    """A tiny scale pushes |O * sigmoid(G) / scale| past 448: ``cvt.rn.satfinite`` stores +-448 (torch's cast would give NaN from 480 up), the
+    sign kept, no NaN byte; inside the range the twin's bytes stay within one ulp -- in both conventions (the staged twin's pre-cast value is the
+    stack convention's ``bf16(a / (1 + exp(-g))) * inv`` on the ungated bf16 O)."""
+    from cudnn.sdpa.fwd.kernels.sm100 import split_combine as comb
+
+    b, h, sq, d, splits = 1, 24, 4, 256, 65
+    op, lp, ref_o, ref_lse = _partials(b, h, sq, d, splits)
+    gate = _gate(b, sq, h, d, torch.bfloat16, 3)
+    scale = torch.tensor([2e-4], dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda")  # inv 5000: |O * sigmoid(G)| above 0.096 saturates -- most live elements
+    fused = _entries(comb, fused=True, tag="bf16", rounding=rounding, forms=("auto",))["auto"]
+    twin = _entries(comb, fused=False, tag="bf16", forms=("auto",))["auto"]
+    o, lse = _launch(fused, op, lp, b, h, sq, d, splits, gate, scale=scale)
+    ot, lt = _launch(twin, op, lp, b, h, sq, d, splits, gate, out_dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    f = o.cpu().float()
+    live = _live_rows(ref_lse).unsqueeze(-1).expand_as(f)
+    assert not torch.isnan(f).any() and torch.equal(lse, lt)
+    if rounding == "single":
+        pre = ot.cpu().float() * (1.0 / scale.cpu().float().item())  # the twin's pre-cast value
+    else:
+        oa, la = _launch(_plain_entries(comb, forms=("auto",))["auto"], op, lp, b, h, sq, d, splits, None, out_dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        assert torch.equal(la, lt)
+        inv = torch.ones((), dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda") / scale.reshape(())
+        pre = ((oa.float() / (1.0 + torch.exp(-gate.float()))).to(torch.bfloat16).float() * inv).cpu()  # the stack convention's pre-cast value
+    over = (pre.abs() >= 480.0) & live  # beyond torch's NaN threshold: ours must read exactly +-448
+    inside = (pre.abs() < 400.0) & live
+    assert over.sum() > 1000 and inside.sum() > 100, f"the cell must exercise both sides: {int(over.sum())} elements past 480, {int(inside.sum())} inside"
+    assert torch.equal(f[over], torch.sign(pre[over]) * E4M3_MAX), "saturated elements read +-448 exactly"
+    hist = _histogram(_ulp_distance(f[inside], pre[inside].to(torch.float8_e4m3fn).float()))
+    print(f"\nsaturation cell ({rounding}): {int(over.sum())} saturated, inside the range {hist}")
+    assert hist["more"] == 0
+    assert torch.count_nonzero(f[~live]).item() == 0

+def _adapter_fused_cell(*, tile_form, split, B, SQ, kv_lens, paged, seed, out_rounding="single"):
+    """The ``tile_form`` route (``split`` 0 = the body's default: the lean tile's 65 at k 1) with an e4m3 ``o`` + ``out_scale`` + the gate against
+    the same route with a bf16 ``o`` and torch's cast: within one ulp on the live rows, dead rows 0, the LSE bitwise, the combine form the part's
+    own rule names (read back), two launches bitwise.  Under ``out_rounding="staged"`` the reference is the stack-convention model on the same
+    route's UNGATED bf16 ``o`` (one more run; its LSE bitwise the gated run's).  Returns ``(histogram, combine form)``."""
+    import test_sdpa_fwd_sparse_sm107 as S
+    from cudnn.sdpa.fwd.sparse_gqa_sm107 import SparseGqaFwdDslSm107, _sparse_combine_decode_grid
+    import cuda.bindings.driver as cuda
+
+    D, H, KH, top_k, dtype = 256, 24, 2, 512, torch.bfloat16
+    q, kk, vv, g = S._inputs(B, SQ, H, KH, dtype, seed, SKV=8192)
+    ids, lens = S._decode_lists("shuffled", B, SQ, top_k, kv_lens, g)
+    scale_sm = 1.0 / math.sqrt(D)
+    ref_o, ref_lse, _ = S._reference_decode(q, kk, vv, ids, lens, kv_lens, scale_sm, top_k)
+    gate = (torch.randn(B, SQ, H, D, generator=g, device=q.device, dtype=torch.float32) * 2.0).to(dtype)
+    out_scale = torch.tensor([0.05], dtype=torch.float32, device=q.device)
+    seq_kv = torch.tensor(kv_lens, device=q.device, dtype=torch.int32)
+    kw = {}
+    if paged is not None:
+        P, hnd = paged
+        kp, vp, table = S._paginate(kk, vv, kv_lens, P, hnd, "nan", g)
+        kk, vv = kp, vp
+        kw = dict(paged_kv=True, page_size=P, block_table=table)
+    if split:
+        kw["split_kv"] = split
+    stream = cuda.CUstream(int(torch.cuda.current_stream().cuda_stream))
+
+    def run(o_dtype, launches, gated=True):
+        outs, a = [], None
+        fused_o = o_dtype == torch.float8_e4m3fn
+        for _ in range(launches):
+            o = torch.full((B, SQ, H, D), E4M3_MAX if fused_o else 1.5e30, device=q.device, dtype=o_dtype)
+            lse = torch.full((B, H, SQ), 1.5e30, device=q.device, dtype=torch.float32)
+            a = SparseGqaFwdDslSm107(
+                q=q,
+                k=kk,
+                v=vv,
+                o=o,
+                lse=lse,
+                block_ids=ids,
+                block_lens=lens,
+                seq_kv_lens=seq_kv,
+                top_k=top_k,
+                scale=scale_sm,
+                list_per_sequence=True,
+                bottom_right=True,
+                epilogue_gate=gate if gated else None,
+                tile_form=tile_form,
+                out_scale=out_scale if fused_o else None,
+                out_rounding=out_rounding if fused_o else "single",
+                **kw,
+            )
+            assert a.check_support()
+            with process_watchdog(300, f"adapter {tile_form} route (fused e4m3) compile + first dispatch"):
+                a.compile()
+                ws = torch.full((max(a.scratch_workspace_bytes(), 16) // 4,), 1.5e30, device=q.device, dtype=torch.float32)
+                a.execute(stream=stream, workspace=ws)
+                torch.cuda.synchronize()
+            outs.append((o, lse))
+        return outs, a
+
+    fused, af = run(torch.float8_e4m3fn, 2)
+    half, ah = run(torch.bfloat16, 1)
+    cc = torch.cuda.get_device_capability(q.device)
+    want_split = split or 65
+    # the part's OWN rule: cc 10.7 and (for a lean plan) cc 10.0 the split-aware rule, cc 10.3 the module's own forms, the tcgen05 body as before
+    want_form = _sparse_combine_decode_grid(B, H, SQ, want_split, cc, lean=(tile_form == "lean"))
+    assert af.fused_e4m3 and not ah.fused_e4m3 and af.tile_form == ah.tile_form == tile_form and af.split_kv == ah.split_kv == want_split
+    assert af.combine_form() == ah.combine_form() == want_form == af._combine_form, (cc, want_form)
+    assert af.out_rounding == out_rounding and ah.out_rounding == "single"
+    (o1, l1), (o2, l2) = fused
+    assert torch.equal(o1.view(torch.uint8), o2.view(torch.uint8)) and torch.equal(l1, l2), "two launches bitwise"
+    S._check([half[0]], ref_o * torch.sigmoid(gate.float()), ref_lse)  # the bf16 route against the gated oracle (the suite's own check)
+    if out_rounding == "single":

+def test_decode_tile_batch_one_prices_every_partial_of_the_combine(monkeypatch):
+    """Batch 1 x 2 KV heads (2 units) on a 212-SM part under the LEAN combine kernel
+    (no combine grid given, or a grid the lean kernel serves): the combine is one wave
+    of warps walking the split axis serially, so every partial costs it a step
+    (COMBINE_PER_PARTIAL). Measured optima of kernel + combine (grouped-load
+    combine, 2376 MHz lock): kv 4K 16 (14.6 us), kv 32K 32 (24.1), kv 128K 64
+    (41.6); 8 units (batch 4) x 128K 16 (96.8). Without the term the model took
+    64 at kv 32K (26.0 us measured) and 64 at kv 128K with the old combine
+    (68.3 us against 61.1 at 32).  The cc 10.7 row prices every partial of its LEAN
+    forms at that measured rate (decode_tile_combine_per_partial, the row's ``per_split``:
+    the same number the line reads by default, so the picks below hold with and without
+    it); the Blackwell line carries its own fit."""
+    import cudnn.sdpa.fwd.heuristics as heur
+
+    assert _decode_tile(2, 4096, sm_count=212) == 16
+    assert _decode_tile(2, 32768, sm_count=212) == 32
+    assert _decode_tile(2, 131072, sm_count=212) == 64
+    assert _decode_tile(8, 131072, sm_count=212) == 16
+    # a grid the lean kernel serves (a large-batch decode: B 32 x 24 heads = 768 lean blocks) prices the same way
+    assert _decode_tile(2, 32768, sm_count=212, combine_grid=(32, 24, 1)) == 32
+    # the captured caller (no launch term) keeps the same splits at these shapes
+    assert _decode_tile(2, 32768, sm_count=212, launch_cost=0.0) == 32
+    assert _decode_tile(2, 131072, sm_count=212, launch_cost=0.0) == 64
+
+    def rubin(units, s_kv, **kw):
+        return _decode_tile(units, s_kv, sm_count=212, per_split=heur._DECODE_TILE_COMBINE_PER_PARTIAL, **kw)
+
+    assert rubin(2, 4096) == 16
+    assert rubin(2, 32768) == 32
+    assert rubin(2, 131072) == 64
+    assert rubin(8, 131072) == 16
+    # the captured caller (no launch term) keeps the same splits at these shapes
+    assert rubin(2, 32768, launch_cost=0.0) == 32
+    assert rubin(2, 131072, launch_cost=0.0) == 64

+    # makes every finer split free once the loop term stops paying for it -- the 40 us combine measured behind a 12 us kernel)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(heur, "_DECODE_TILE_COMBINE_PER_PARTIAL", 0.0)
+    assert rubin(2, 32768) == 64
+    assert rubin(2, 131072) == 64

+def test_decode_tile_serial_combine_bounds_the_split_depth():
+    """One KV head at 128k keys (1024 tiles, 1 unit): with no per-split term the
+    model took 128 splits at every S_q.  At S_q >= 3 the serial combine pays
+    ~0.45 us a split, so the 128-split pass alone was ~60 of the measured 72 us
+    (qwen3.5-tp8 b=1 q=4 on B300, 1.5x behind the best flashinfer backend).
+    The serial term caps it; the decode form's smaller term still lets the
+    one-row launch split deep, and the saturated serving shape is untouched."""

+    decode = _blackwell_tile(1, 131072)

+    assert decode >= serial, (decode, serial)
+    assert decode >= 32, decode

+def test_decode_tile_prices_the_combine_by_the_form_its_grid_takes():
+    """The combine's per-partial price depends on which kernel the launch takes, and that is
+    decided by the combine GRID (``combine_grid`` = the graph's (B, H_q, S_q): the lean kernel's
+    ceil(S_q / 4) x H_q x B blocks, :func:`decode_combine_lean_blocks`, bound which launches
+    change at all; the rows S_q x H_q x B, :func:`decode_combine_rows`, are what the decode-grid
+    kernel's own time grows with): the DECODE-GRID kernel spreads the
+    split axis over eight lane chains, so its time is FLAT in the split count -- measured on
+    the Rubin performance class at B 1 x 24 heads: 2.0-2.1 us (S_q 1) / 2.4-2.7 (S_q 4)
+    standalone from 4 to 128 splits, 3.1-3.7 us in the step, a slope of 0.0004-0.009 us per
+    partial against the lean kernel's 0.127-0.177 -- so a batch-1 launch on it splits as deep
+    as the stream saturation allows.  Measured step optima with the decode-grid combine at
+    B 1 x 24 heads: kv 32K 64 (14.4 us against 23.4 at the lean split 32), kv 128K 64 (30.6),
+    B 4 x kv 128K 16 (94.1); the lean form's picks (the test above) are unchanged.  The
+    decode-grid intercept grows with the ROWS (standalone 2.08 / 2.4 / 4.93 us at 24 / 96 / 384
+    rows: B 1 x S_q 1, B 1 x S_q 4 = B 4 x S_q 1, B 4 x S_q 4 at 24 heads), which keeps a
+    mid-sized grid from splitting past what its combine saves."""
+    import cudnn.sdpa.fwd.heuristics as heur
+
+    assert (
+        heur.decode_combine_lean_blocks(1, 24, 1) == 24  # one row per block at S_q 1: the lean grid is per (head, batch)
+        and heur.decode_combine_lean_blocks(4, 24, 4) == 96
+        and heur.decode_combine_lean_blocks(2, 4, 1024) == 2048
+        and heur.decode_combine_rows(1, 24, 1) == 24
+        and heur.decode_combine_rows(1, 24, 4) == heur.decode_combine_rows(4, 24, 1) == 96
+        and heur.decode_combine_rows(4, 24, 4) == 384
+    )
+    assert heur._DECODE_TILE_COMBINE_PER_PARTIAL_DECODE_GRID < heur._DECODE_TILE_COMBINE_PER_PARTIAL
+    six = dict(sm_count=212, combine_grid=(1, 24, 1))
+    assert _decode_tile(2, 32768, **six) == 64 and _decode_tile(2, 32768, launch_cost=0.0, **six) == 64
+    assert _decode_tile(2, 131072, **six) == 64 and _decode_tile(2, 131072, launch_cost=0.0, **six) == 64
+    assert _decode_tile(8, 131072, sm_count=212, combine_grid=(4, 24, 1)) == 16
+    # the price is the form's, not the batch's: the lean form at the same shapes keeps the lean picks
+    assert _decode_tile(2, 32768, sm_count=212, combine_grid=(128, 32, 1)) == 32
+    # the combine price per partial is what the form changes: the decode-grid intercept at a small grid is the lean one
+    assert heur._decode_tile_combine_cost(64, grid=(1, 24, 1)) < heur._decode_tile_combine_cost(64, grid=None)
+    assert heur._decode_tile_combine_cost(64, grid=(1, 24, 1)) == pytest.approx(
+        heur._DECODE_TILE_COMBINE_COST + 64 * heur._DECODE_TILE_COMBINE_PER_PARTIAL_DECODE_GRID
+    )
+    assert heur._decode_tile_combine_cost(64, grid=None) == pytest.approx(heur._DECODE_TILE_COMBINE_COST + 64 * heur._DECODE_TILE_COMBINE_PER_PARTIAL)
+    # the row-count term of the decode-grid intercept: flat up to the small-grid bound (96 rows either way), growing past it
+    assert heur._decode_tile_combine_cost(64, grid=(4, 24, 1)) == pytest.approx(heur._decode_tile_combine_cost(64, grid=(1, 24, 4)))
+    assert heur._decode_tile_combine_cost(64, grid=(1, 24, 4)) == pytest.approx(heur._decode_tile_combine_cost(64, grid=(1, 24, 1)))
+    assert heur._decode_tile_combine_cost(64, grid=(4, 24, 4)) > heur._decode_tile_combine_cost(64, grid=(4, 24, 1))

+def test_decode_combine_form_rule_is_split_aware_at_the_crossover():
+    """Which combine kernel a split launch takes (``decode_combine_grid_selected``), measured on the
+    Rubin performance class with the combine alone at 24 heads: the decode-grid kernel is flat in
+    the split count but costs more blocks per row, so on a SMALL grid (up to 128 rows: B 1 x S_q 1
+    = 24 rows, B 1 x S_q 4 and B 4 x S_q 1 = 96) it wins from split 8 on (2.1-2.5 us against the
+    lean kernel's 3.4-18 us) and loses only at split 4 (by 0.03-0.4 us), while at B 4 x S_q 4
+    (384 rows) its 4.9-5.4 us loses to the lean walk up to split 16 (3.9 us) and wins from
+    split 32 (6.0 us) -- the crossover is near 23.  The rule: the decode-grid kernel when the
+    launch is inside the kernel module's own grid bound (``DECODE_COMBINE_MAX_LEAN_BLOCKS`` lean
+    blocks), the split is at least ``DECODE_COMBINE_MIN_SPLIT`` (8), and the grid is small or the
+    split at least ``DECODE_COMBINE_DEEP_SPLIT`` (32); the lean kernel otherwise.  The kernel
+    module's own entry takes the decode-grid kernel on every launch inside its bound, so
+    ``decode_combine_force_lean`` names exactly the launches the adapter must pin to the lean
+    kernel; a launch outside the bound is the lean kernel's by construction either way."""
+    from cudnn.sdpa.fwd import heuristics as heur
+
+    assert (heur.DECODE_COMBINE_MIN_SPLIT, heur.DECODE_COMBINE_DEEP_SPLIT, heur.DECODE_COMBINE_SMALL_GRID_ROWS) == (8, 32, 128)
+    sel, force = heur.decode_combine_grid_selected, heur.decode_combine_force_lean
+    # the B 4 x S_q 4 crossover (384 rows, 96 lean blocks): lean up to 16, the decode-grid kernel from 32
+    assert [sel(4, 24, 4, s) for s in (4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128)] == [False, False, False, True, True, True]
+    assert [force(4, 24, 4, s) for s in (4, 8, 16, 32, 64)] == [True, True, True, False, False]
+    # the small grids: B 1 x S_q 1 (24 rows), B 1 x S_q 4 and B 4 x S_q 1 (96 rows): the decode-grid kernel from split 8
+    for grid in ((1, 24, 1), (1, 24, 4), (4, 24, 1), (1, 32, 1), (4, 32, 1)):
+        assert [sel(*grid, s) for s in (2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128)] == [False, False, True, True, True, True, True], grid
+        assert force(*grid, 4) and not force(*grid, 8) and not force(*grid, 64), grid
+    # the band between (more than 128 rows inside the kernel's bound): the deep splits only
+    for grid in ((2, 32, 4), (4, 32, 4), (2, 24, 8), (4, 32, 2)):
+        assert [sel(*grid, s) for s in (8, 16, 32, 64)] == [False, False, True, True], grid
+        assert force(*grid, 16) and not force(*grid, 32), grid
+    # past the kernel module's bound (B 8 x 32 heads x S_q 1 = 256 lean blocks; a prefill grid): the lean kernel by
+    # construction, nothing to force
+    for grid in ((8, 32, 1), (32, 24, 1), (128, 24, 4), (2, 4, 1024)):
+        assert not any(sel(*grid, s) for s in (8, 32, 64, 128)) and not any(force(*grid, s) for s in (4, 16, 64)), grid
+    # exactly at the bound (B 4 x 32 heads x S_q 1 = 128 lean blocks = 128 rows): a small grid
+    assert sel(4, 32, 1, 8) and sel(4, 32, 1, 16) and not sel(4, 32, 1, 4)
+    # the split model prices the crossover cell by the rule: B 4 x 24/2 x kv 4K x S_q 4 on the 64-column tile stays at 16
+    # (its lean combine) rather than jumping to the decode-grid kernel's deep splits
+    assert _decode_tile(8, 4096, sm_count=212, q_tile=64, combine_grid=(4, 24, 4)) == 16
+    assert heur._decode_tile_combine_cost(16, grid=(4, 24, 4)) == pytest.approx(heur._decode_tile_combine_cost(16, grid=None))
+    assert heur._decode_tile_combine_cost(32, grid=(4, 24, 4)) < heur._decode_tile_combine_cost(32, grid=None)
+

+"""``tile_dsl.pointwise.bf16_words_to_e4m3_words`` -- the e4m3 rounding OF A PACKED bf16 ROW: four ``bf16x2`` words (8 elements) into two
+``e4m3x4`` words, each bf16 widened to fp32 EXACTLY (a bit move) and rounded ONCE by ``cvt.rn.satfinite.e4m3x2.f32``, element order preserved.
+The contract: the two words are bitwise ``bf16_row.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)`` -- the convention of the indexer's e4m3 compressed-key cache

+def _run_probe(tmp_path, *, arch: str, fused: bool, e5m2: bool, src: int = SRC_GMEM, timeout: int = 900):
+    """Trace-compile the probe for ``arch`` in a fresh interpreter (CUTE_DSL_DUMP_DIR must be set before ``import cutlass``)."""
+    tag = f"{arch}_{'fused' if fused else 'unfused'}_{'e5m2' if e5m2 else 'e4m3'}_src{src}"

+# Tier 2: numerics on a Rubin device
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+_E4M3_MAX, _E5M2_MAX = 448.0, 57344.0
+_FP32_MIN_NORMAL = 2.0**-126
+
+
+def _f32(bits: int) -> float:
+    return struct.unpack("<f", struct.pack("<I", bits))[0]
+
+
+def e8m0_descale(e: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """``2^(127 - e)`` as fp32: ``e = 254 -> 2^-127`` (the fp32 subnormal 0x00400000), ``e = 255 -> NaN`` (the e8m0 NaN)."""
+    e64 = e.to(torch.int64)
+    bits = torch.where(e64 == 254, torch.full_like(e64, 0x00400000), (254 - e64) << 23)
+    bits = torch.where(e64 == 255, torch.full_like(e64, 0x7FC00000), bits)
+    return bits.to(torch.int32).view(torch.float32)
+
+
+def torch_scaled_pack(x: torch.Tensor, e: torch.Tensor, fmt: str, *, ftz_inputs: bool) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """The torch DEscale oracle of the instruction: ``fp8(x * 2^(127-e))`` per element, e5m2 clamped to +-57344 first (torch's
+    e5m2 cast does not saturate; e4m3fn's does), NaN passed through (0x7f), ``e = 255`` -> 0x7f in EVERY byte, and --
+    with ``ftz_inputs`` -- fp32-subnormal inputs flushed to signed zero, which is what the hardware does.  ``x``:
+    ``[n, k]`` fp32, ``e``: ``[n]`` int; returns uint8 ``[n, k]``."""
+    x = x.float()
+    if ftz_inputs:
+        sub = (x != 0) & (x.abs() < _FP32_MIN_NORMAL)
+        x = torch.where(sub, torch.copysign(torch.zeros_like(x), x), x)
+    y = x * e8m0_descale(e).unsqueeze(-1)
+    m = _E4M3_MAX if fmt == "e4m3" else _E5M2_MAX
+    y = torch.where(torch.isnan(y), y, y.clamp(-m, m))
+    dt = torch.float8_e4m3fn if fmt == "e4m3" else torch.float8_e5m2
+    b = y.to(dt).view(torch.uint8)
+    return torch.where((e == 255).unsqueeze(-1), torch.full_like(b, 0x7F), b)
+
+
+# Edge lanes (one 16-value block + its scale byte each); the rest of the lanes are random normal fp32 with e in [0, 253].
+_EDGE_A = [1.0, -1.0, 17.0, 19.0, 21.0, 23.0, 448.0, 449.0, 464.0, 1000.0, 3e38, -3e38, 2.0**-9, 1.5 * 2.0**-10, 2.0**-10, 0.0]
+_EDGE_B = [
+    float("inf"),
+    -float("inf"),
+    float("nan"),
+    -0.0,
+    57344.0,
+    61440.0,
+    -1e6,
+    1e-30,
+    2.0**-6,
+    2.0**-7,
+    2.0**-8,
+    2.0**-14,
+    2.0**-16,
+    2.0**-17,
+    1.0625,
+    1.4375,
+]
+_EDGE_SUB = [
+    _f32(0x00080000),
+    _f32(0x000116C2),
+    -_f32(0x00080000),
+    2.0**-130,
+    1e-40,
+    -1e-40,
+    2.0**-127,
+    2.0**-140,
+    1.0,
+    2.0,
+    0.0,
+    -0.0,
+    448.0,
+    0.5,
+    2.0**-6,
+    3.0,
+]
+_EDGE_LANES = [
+    # (values, e, tag)
+    (_EDGE_A, 127, "identity scale, ties, saturation, min subnormal"),
+    (_EDGE_B, 127, "inf / NaN / signed zero / e5m2 range"),
+    (_EDGE_A, 255, "e8m0 NaN byte -> 0x7f7f"),
+    (_EDGE_B, 255, "e8m0 NaN byte -> 0x7f7f (inf / NaN inputs)"),
+    ([2.0**-118, 1e-30, 1.0, 2.0, -(2.0**-118), 2.0**-120, 2.0**-125, 0.0, 3e38, -1.0, 2.0**-119, 2.0**-118 * 1.5, 0.75, 1e6, -1e6, 7.0], 0, "e = 0 is 2^+127"),
+    ([448.0, 3e38, 1.0, -3e38, 1e30, 2.0**100, 0.0, -0.0, 1e38, -1e38, 2.0**126, 2.0**125, 1.5 * 2.0**126, 2.0**120, 0.5, 1e10], 254, "e = 254 is 2^-127"),
+    (_EDGE_SUB, 0, "fp32-subnormal inputs at e = 0 (fused flushes, FMUL scales)"),
+    (_EDGE_SUB, 1, "fp32-subnormal inputs at e = 1"),
+    (_EDGE_SUB, 2, "fp32-subnormal inputs at e = 2"),
+    (_EDGE_A, P_SF_BYTE, "P's fixed byte 119 = x * 2^8"),
+    (_EDGE_A, 126, "e - 127 = -1 -> x * 2"),
+    (_EDGE_A, 128, "e - 127 = +1 -> x / 2"),
+]

+
+def _device_inputs(n_blocks: int, seed: int = 20260929):
+    n = n_blocks * LANES_PER_BLOCK
+    g = torch.Generator(device="cpu").manual_seed(seed)
+    mag = torch.exp2(torch.rand(n, N_PACK, generator=g) * 60.0 - 30.0)  # |x| log-uniform in 2^-30 .. 2^30: never an fp32 subnormal
+    x = torch.randn(n, N_PACK, generator=g) * mag
+    e = torch.randint(0, 254, (n,), generator=g, dtype=torch.int32)  # [0, 253]: e8m0_rcp's contract
+    for i, (vals, ee, _tag) in enumerate(_EDGE_LANES):
+        x[i] = torch.tensor(vals, dtype=torch.float32)
+        e[i] = ee
+    return x.contiguous(), e.contiguous()
+
+
+def _lane_masks(x: torch.Tensor, e: torch.Tensor):
+    """Which lanes the bit-identity contract covers: no fp32-subnormal input and e <= 253."""
+    has_sub = ((x != 0) & (x.abs() < _FP32_MIN_NORMAL)).any(dim=1)
+    return (~has_sub) & (e <= 253)
+

+def _launch_probe(mod, x, e, *, e5m2: bool, fused: bool, src: int):
+    """One device run of the probe: returns ``(bytes [n, 16] uint8, pair [n] int32, byte_used [n] int32)``."""
+    import cuda.bindings.driver as _cuda_driver
+    import cutlass
+    import cutlass.cute as cute
+    from cutlass.cute.runtime import from_dlpack
+
+    dev = x.device
+    n = x.shape[0]
+    n_blocks = n // LANES_PER_BLOCK
+    dst = torch.full((n, N_PACK // 4), -1, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
+    pair = torch.full((n,), -1, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
+    sf_out = torch.full((n,), -1, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
+    stream = _cuda_driver.CUstream(torch.cuda.current_stream(dev).cuda_stream)
+    args = (
+        from_dlpack(x, assumed_align=16),
+        from_dlpack(e, assumed_align=16),
+        from_dlpack(dst, assumed_align=16),
+        from_dlpack(pair, assumed_align=16),
+        from_dlpack(sf_out, assumed_align=16),
+        cutlass.Int32(P_SF_BYTE),
+        cutlass.Int32(n_blocks),
+    )
+    fn = cute.compile(mod.launch, *args, e5m2, fused, src, stream)
+    fn(*args, stream)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    assert int((dst == -1).all(dim=1).sum().item()) == 0 and int((pair == -1).sum().item()) == 0, "unwritten lanes"
+    if src in (SRC_PYINT, SRC_TRACED_CONST):
+        sf_out = torch.full((n,), P_SF_BYTE, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)  # the probe stores no byte for a constant source
+    else:
+        assert int((sf_out == -1).sum().item()) == 0, "the probe must store the byte every lane used"
+    return dst.view(torch.uint8).reshape(n, N_PACK), pair, sf_out
+

+        pytest.skip(f"compiled + PTX pinned; SASS half skipped: {[ln for ln in lines if ln.startswith(('SKIP', 'REJECT'))]}")
+    sass = {ln.split()[1]: int(ln.split()[2]) for ln in lines if ln.startswith("SASS ")}
+    print(f"\nfp8 x4 scaled pairs sm_107a PTX {ptx} SASS {sass} (MOV R,UR = {sass['MOV_R_UR']}: the uniform-register floor, one per CREDUX)")
+    assert sass["CREDUX"] == N_COLS, sass
+    assert sass["SCALE_BY_C"] == N_COLS, f"the fused arm is one SCALE_BY_C per element -- {sass}"
+    assert sass["PLAIN_E4M3"] == N_COLS // 2, f"the FMUL arm is one plain pair cvt per two elements -- {sass}"
+    assert sass["E8M0_CVT"] == N_COLS, sass
+    assert sass["FMUL2"] >= N_COLS // 2, f"e8m0_pair_u's packed multiplies -- {sass}"

+
+def _f32(bits: int) -> float:
+    return struct.unpack("<f", struct.pack("<I", bits))[0]
+
+
+def ue8m0_rp(scaled: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """``cvt.rp.satfinite.ue8m0x2.f32`` of a finite non-negative fp32: the smallest power of two >= ``scaled`` as a biased exponent
+    (``0 -> 0x00``; a power of two is its own exponent; saturates at 254).  Exact through ``frexp`` (no log2 rounding)."""
+    m, k = torch.frexp(scaled)  # scaled = m * 2^k, m in [0.5, 1)
+    e = torch.where(m == 0.5, k - 1, k) + 127  # ceil(log2(scaled)) + 127
+    e = torch.where(scaled == 0, torch.zeros_like(e), e)
+    return e.clamp(0, 254).to(torch.int32)
+
+
+def torch_oracle(x: torch.Tensor):
+    """``x``: ``[n_warps, 32, 64]`` fp32.  Returns ``(e [n_warps, 64] int32, words [n_warps, 32, 16] int32)`` = the per-column E8M0
+    byte of the rule ``ue8m0_rp(amax * fp32(1/448))`` and the e4m3 payload ``e4m3_rn_satfinite(x * 2^(127 - e))``, element i in byte
+    i of word i // 4."""
+    amax = x.abs().amax(dim=1)  # [n_warps, 64]
+    scaled = amax * torch.tensor(_f32(E8M0_RCP_E4M3_MAX_BITS), dtype=torch.float32, device=x.device)
+    e = ue8m0_rp(scaled)
+    descale = ((254 - e.to(torch.int64)) << 23).to(torch.int32).view(torch.float32)  # 2^(127 - e), e <= 253 on these inputs
+    y = (x * descale.unsqueeze(1)).clamp(-448.0, 448.0)
+    b = y.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn).view(torch.uint8)  # [n_warps, 32, 64]
+    words = b.reshape(x.shape[0], 32, 16, 4).to(torch.int32)
+    words = words[..., 0] | (words[..., 1] << 8) | (words[..., 2] << 16) | (words[..., 3] << 24)
+    return e, words
+
+
+def _inputs(n_warps: int, seed: int = 20261001) -> torch.Tensor:
+    g = torch.Generator(device="cpu").manual_seed(seed)
+    mag = torch.exp2(torch.rand(n_warps, 1, N_COLS, generator=g) * 40.0 - 20.0)  # per column magnitude 2^-20 .. 2^20 (never an fp32 subnormal)
+    x = torch.randn(n_warps, 32, N_COLS, generator=g) * mag
+    x[0, :, :4] = 0.0  # an all-zero column block: byte 0x00, payload 0
+    x[1, 0, 8] = 448.0  # a block amax exactly 448: scaled == 1.0 -> e = 127 (the power-of-two corner)
+    x[1, 1:, 8] = 0.0
+    x[1, 0, 9] = 449.0  # just above: e = 128
+    x[1, 1:, 9] = 0.0
+    return x.contiguous()
+
+
+@requires_rubin
+def test_pairs_and_payload_match_the_shipped_rule_and_the_oracle_on_device(tmp_path):
+    import cuda.bindings.driver as _cuda_driver
+    import cutlass
+    import cutlass.cute as cute
+    from cutlass.cute.runtime import from_dlpack
+
+    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("_fp8_x4_scaled_pairs_probe_device", str(_write_probe(tmp_path)))
+    mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+    spec.loader.exec_module(mod)
+    dev = torch.device("cuda")
+    n_warps = 256
+    x = _inputs(n_warps).to(dev)
+    fused = torch.full((n_warps * 32 * 16,), -1, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
+    unfused = torch.full_like(fused, -1)
+    pair_u = torch.full((n_warps * 32 * 32,), -1, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
+    pair_ref = torch.full_like(pair_u, -1)
+    stream = _cuda_driver.CUstream(torch.cuda.current_stream(dev).cuda_stream)
+    args = (
+        from_dlpack(x.reshape(-1), assumed_align=16),
+        from_dlpack(fused, assumed_align=16),
+        from_dlpack(unfused, assumed_align=16),
+        from_dlpack(pair_u, assumed_align=16),
+        from_dlpack(pair_ref, assumed_align=16),
+        cutlass.Int32(n_warps),

+    cute.compile(mod.launch, *args, stream)(*args, stream)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()

+    unfused = unfused.reshape(n_warps, 32, 16)
+    pair_u = pair_u.reshape(n_warps, 32, 32)
+    pair_ref = pair_ref.reshape(n_warps, 32, 32)
+    assert int((pair_u == -1).sum()) == 0 and int((pair_ref == -1).sum()) == 0, "unwritten pair words"
+    # (1) e8m0_pair_u == e8m0_pair bitwise on every (lane, pair): the same rule, op for op

+    # the pair words are warp-uniform

+"""``tile_dsl.tma.tma_gather4`` / ``ldg_int32x4`` / ``opaque_i64`` -- the index-list row gather of a d = 256 K/V tile.
+
+The primitive lands four indirectly-addressed rows of a 2-D tensor map per issue in the SAME SWIZZLE_128B layout a tiled
+box load produces, provided every quad sits at a 512-B-aligned offset inside a 1024-B-aligned sub-box.  That claim has no
+symptom when it is wrong (the bytes are finite and plausible), so it is pinned through the STORE path: the roundtrip probe
+(``tile_dsl_gather4_probe.py``) gathers 64 KiB tiles (32 blocks of 4 token rows x 4 column boxes of 128 B) from a
+``[S, H_kv * 256]`` bf16 table with the head in the COLUMN coordinate, TMA-stores each tile through a plain tiled
+(128, 64) SWIZZLE_128B box and the test compares with ``kv[4 blk + r, h * 256 : (h + 1) * 256]`` bitwise.
+
+Three tiers:
+
+* host, no device: the primitive imports nothing kernel-private and nothing of the pre-upstream DSL; the ``cta_group``
+  contract; the CuTe DSL version gate (AGENTS.md Rule 7) -- a DSL below the floor and a DSL without the ``sm_107a``
+  target are each refused by NAME, before any atom import (a controlled probe over the version state, no real downgrade);
+  the HOST entry of that gate is ``tile_dsl.requirements`` (no cutlass import -- ``test_tile_dsl_requirements.py`` proves
+  it importable below the floor in a fresh process, which the probes here, run after importing ``tma``, cannot).
+* host, an ``sm_107a`` trace-compile (any box whose cutlass-dsl knows the arch): the PTX carries one
+  ``tile::gather4 ... cta_group::N.L2::cache_hint`` per issue of the per-warp body, the ``ld.global.nc.v4.s32`` id load and
+  the opaque ``mov.b64`` of the EVICT_LAST hint; with an nvdisasm that decodes the cubin, the SASS carries one
+  ``UTMALDG.2D.GATHER4`` per issue (the ``.2CTA`` form under ``cta_group=2``), ``R2UR`` (the elected-lane issue model) and
+  no spill.
+* ``requires_rubin`` (a cc 10.7 device): the roundtrip, bitwise, with ``-1`` and past-the-end block ids coming back as
+  four ZERO rows -- their bytes are credited (an uncredited OOB row hangs the ``expect_tx`` = the full share, exit 124
+  under ``timeout``) and not over-credited (the same mbarrier serves a second tile on its next phase, bitwise too); the
+  8-warp form of the sparse core, the 4-warp fallback, one CTA per SM, and the ``cta_group=2`` pair-leader routing (the
+  non-leader's local mbarrier must NOT complete).  Skips typed below the DSL floor and on a DSL without ``sm_107a``.

+def _stream():
+    """The current torch stream as a ``CUstream`` for the compiled probe."""

+def _skip_unless_the_dsl_serves_this_part():

+    from cudnn.frost.tile_dsl.requirements import tma_gather4_requirement_error

+def _block_ids(n_tiles: int, n_blocks_kv: int, *, g: torch.Generator) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Random block ids per tile with the degenerate rows planted: ``-1`` (no key) every 7th slot, the past-the-end block
+    ``n_blocks_kv`` on some of them, and one tile whose 32 slots are ALL ``-1`` (the clamped dead item of the sparse core)."""
+    P = _probe()
+    ids = torch.randint(0, n_blocks_kv, (n_tiles, P.N_BLOCKS), generator=g, dtype=torch.int64)
+    flat = ids.reshape(-1)
+    flat[::7] = -1
+    flat[3::21] = n_blocks_kv
+    ids[n_tiles // 2] = -1
+    return ids.to(torch.int32)
+
+
+def _expected(kv2d: torch.Tensor, ids: torch.Tensor, heads: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """``out[tile * 128 + 4 blk + r] = kv2d[4 ids[tile, blk] + r, h * D : (h + 1) * D]`` when that row exists, else zeros."""
+    P = _probe()
+    S = kv2d.shape[0]
+    n_tiles = ids.shape[0]
+    rows = (ids.to(torch.int64) * P.BLOCK).unsqueeze(-1) + torch.arange(P.BLOCK, device=ids.device)  # [tiles, 32, 4]
+    rows = rows.reshape(n_tiles, P.TILE_ROWS)
+    live = (rows >= 0) & (rows < S)
+    cols = heads.to(torch.int64).unsqueeze(-1) * P.D + torch.arange(P.D, device=ids.device)  # [tiles, D]
+    gathered = kv2d[rows.clamp(0, S - 1).unsqueeze(-1), cols.unsqueeze(1)]  # [tiles, 128, D]
+    want = torch.where(live.unsqueeze(-1), gathered, torch.zeros((), dtype=kv2d.dtype, device=kv2d.device))
+    return want.reshape(n_tiles * P.TILE_ROWS, P.D)
+
+
+_S = 4096  # table rows (tokens) of every roundtrip case: 1024 blocks of 4
+
+
+def _run_roundtrip(h_kv: int, gw: int, cta_group: int, n_cta: int, n_tiles: int = 2, *, seed: int = 0):
+    """Gather ``n_tiles`` tiles per CTA from a random table through the probe; returns the probe module, the table, the ids and the outputs."""
+    P = _probe()
+    dev = torch.device("cuda")
+    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
+    kv2d = torch.randn(_S, h_kv * P.D, generator=g).to(torch.bfloat16).to(dev)
+    ids = _block_ids(n_cta * n_tiles, _S // P.BLOCK, g=g).to(dev)
+    heads = (torch.arange(n_cta * n_tiles, device=dev) // n_tiles) % h_kv  # the probe's head = bidx % H_KV
+    out = torch.full((n_cta * n_tiles * P.TILE_ROWS, P.D), 3.0, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev)  # a sentinel no gathered row carries
+    probe = torch.full((n_cta * n_tiles * 2,), -9, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
+    art = P.compile_roundtrip(h_kv, gw, cta_group)
+    import cutlass
+
+    ids_flat = ids.reshape(-1).contiguous()  # the kernel reads the ids as one flat row-major [tiles * 32] int32 stream
+    art(kv2d, out, ids_flat, probe, cutlass.Int32(n_cta), cutlass.Int32(n_tiles), _stream())
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    want = _expected(kv2d, ids, heads)
+    out2 = torch.zeros_like(out)
+    probe2 = torch.zeros_like(probe)
+    art(kv2d, out2, ids_flat, probe2, cutlass.Int32(n_cta), cutlass.Int32(n_tiles), _stream())
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    return ids, out, want, probe.cpu().view(-1, 2), out2
+

+def _assert_bitwise(out, want, ids, label):
+    """Bitwise comparison of a gathered tile against ``kv[ids]``, naming the first mismatching rows and their block ids."""
+    P = _probe()
+    bad = (out != want).any(dim=1).nonzero().flatten()
+    if bad.numel():
+        first = bad[:8].tolist()
+        blk = [(int(r) // P.TILE_ROWS, (int(r) % P.TILE_ROWS) // P.BLOCK) for r in first]
+        pytest.fail(f"{label}: {bad.numel()} of {out.shape[0]} rows differ; first rows {first} = (tile, block) {blk}, ids {[int(ids[t, b]) for t, b in blk]}")
+
+
+@requires_rubin
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "h_kv, gw, n_cta",
+    [
+        pytest.param(2, 8, 6, id="H_kv2-8warps"),  # the sparse core's form: 8 gather warps, the head in the column coordinate
+        pytest.param(1, 4, 3, id="H_kv1-4warps"),  # the 4-warp fallback over a single-head table
+        pytest.param(2, 8, 0, id="H_kv2-8warps-one-cta-per-sm"),  # n_cta = the SM count
+    ],

+def test_gather4_roundtrip_lands_the_tiled_swizzled_layout(h_kv, gw, n_cta):
+    """gather4 -> the SWIZZLE_128B tile -> tiled TMA store == kv[ids] bitwise, over two tiles per CTA on ONE mbarrier.
+
+    ``-1`` blocks and the past-the-end block come back as four ZERO rows each, with their bytes credited (the arm is the
+    full share; an uncredited row wedges the wait, so a PASS inside the watchdog budget is the credit -- the watchdog ends
+    the process with exit 70 rather than the whole run, as exit 124 under an outer ``timeout`` would) and not over-credited
+    (tile 1 completes on the next phase of the same barrier and is bitwise too); one whole tile of ``-1`` ids is the sparse
+    core's clamped dead item.  The probe pins that the waited phase is complete and the next one is not, and a second
+    launch is bitwise the first."""
+    _skip_unless_the_dsl_serves_this_part()

+    if n_cta == 0:
+        n_cta = torch.cuda.get_device_properties(torch.device("cuda")).multi_processor_count
+    with process_watchdog(420, f"gather4 cta_group=1 roundtrip H_kv={h_kv} gw={gw} n_cta={n_cta}"):
+        ids, out, want, probe, out2 = _run_roundtrip(h_kv, gw, 1, n_cta, seed=h_kv * 10 + gw)
+    idl = ids.to(torch.int64)

+    assert bool(oob[ids.shape[0] // 2].all()), "one tile is all -1 (the dead item)"
+    _assert_bitwise(out, want, ids, f"H_kv={h_kv} gw={gw} n_cta={n_cta}")
+    zero_rows = (out == 0).all(dim=1).view(ids.shape[0], P.N_BLOCKS, P.BLOCK)
+    assert bool(zero_rows[oob].all()), "every OOB block is four zero rows"
+    assert bool((probe[:, 0] == 1).all()), f"every tile's phase completed: {probe.tolist()[:8]}"
+    assert bool((probe[:, 1] == 0).all()), f"no tile's NEXT phase completed (no over-arrival / over-credit): {probe.tolist()[:8]}"
+    assert torch.equal(out, out2), "second launch bitwise"
+    print(f"\ngather4 roundtrip H_kv={h_kv} gw={gw} n_cta={n_cta}: {out.shape[0]} rows bitwise, {int(oob.sum())} OOB blocks zero, 204-SM-class device")
+

+@requires_rubin
+def test_gather4_roundtrip_cta_group_2_credits_the_pair_leader():
+    """Under ``cta_group=2`` ((2,1,1) cluster) ONLY the pair leader arms ``2 x`` its warps' share and waits; both CTAs'
+    tiles come back bitwise (the routing verdict: bytes credited to the leader's copy through the bit-24 clear) and the
+    NON-leader's local mbarrier never completes phase 0 (its parity-1 test reads the fresh-barrier bootstrap TRUE, P2).  A
+    mis-route is a HANG: the watchdog ends the process (exit 70)
+    rather than the whole run; exit 124 under the outer ``timeout`` reads the same."""
+    _skip_unless_the_dsl_serves_this_part()

+    _assert_bitwise(out, want, ids, "cta_group=2")
+    assert torch.equal(out, out2)

+    tile_ix = torch.arange(ids.shape[0])
+    leader = ((tile_ix // tiles_per_cta) % 2) == 0
+    assert bool((probe[leader, 0] == 1).all()) and bool((probe[leader, 1] == 0).all()), f"the pair leaders' mbarriers complete each phase: {probe.tolist()}"
+    # The probe columns are [try_wait.parity(phase), try_wait.parity(phase ^ 1)] with phase = t & 1.  A never-armed barrier stays in
+    # its INITIAL state: the parity-0 test is false (phase 0 never completed) and the parity-1 test is TRUE (the fresh-barrier
+    # bootstrap that lets a `PipelineState.start(phase=1)` wait return at once) -- so the non-leader reads [0, 1] on even tiles and

+    phase = (tile_ix % tiles_per_cta)[~leader] & 1

+"""``tile_dsl.mask.apply_membership_words`` / ``apply_membership_chunk`` -- the per-cell MEMBERSHIP mask of a list-gathered
+KV tile: cell ``c`` keeps ``S[c]`` iff bit ``c % 32`` of word ``c // 32`` is set, else becomes ``-inf`` (a true ``-inf``, so a
+fully-masked chunk's max is ``-inf`` and the consumer's empty-row substitute applies).
+
+Pinned against a torch ``where`` on random words -- including the all-zero word (nothing kept), the all-one word
+(everything kept, kept cells bit-exact), a single-cell word, bit 31 of an ``Int32`` word (the signed encoding
+``-2**31``), a NaN payload passing through a kept cell -- for the 64- and 32-wide two-word form and the 128-wide
+four-word form.  Pure ALU: runs on ANY CUDA device the DSL targets (the trace-time contract tests need no device).
+"""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from frost_test_utils import requires_dsl, requires_sm80
+
+pytestmark = [pytest.mark.L0, requires_dsl]
+
+
+def _stream():
+    """The current torch stream as a ``CUstream`` for the compiled probe."""
+    import cuda.bindings.driver as cuda
+
+    return cuda.CUstream(int(torch.cuda.current_stream().cuda_stream))
+
+
+def _probe():
+    """The probe kernels, built lazily (the cutlass imports must not run at collection on a box without the DSL); the
+    kernel bodies live in this module so the DSL preprocessor can read their source."""
+    import cuda.bindings.driver as cuda
+    import cutlass
+    import cutlass.cute as cute
+    from cutlass.cute.runtime import make_fake_stream, make_fake_tensor
+
+    from cudnn.frost.tile_dsl.mask import apply_membership_chunk, apply_membership_words
+
+    @cute.kernel
+    def membership_kernel(scores: cute.Tensor, words: cute.Tensor, out: cute.Tensor, N: cutlass.Constexpr[int], NW: cutlass.Constexpr[int]):
+        tidx = cutlass.Int32(cute.arch.thread_idx()[0])
+        row = cutlass.Int32(cute.arch.block_idx()[0]) * cutlass.Int32(128) + tidx
+        elems = []
+        for i in cutlass.range_constexpr(N):
+            elems.append(scores[row * N + i])
+        vec = cutlass.Vector.from_elements(tuple(elems), cutlass.Float32)
+        if cutlass.const_expr(NW <= 2):
+            res = apply_membership_chunk(vec, words[row * NW], words[row * NW + 1] if cutlass.const_expr(NW == 2) else words[row * NW], n=N)
+        else:
+            ws = []
+            for s in cutlass.range_constexpr(NW):
+                ws.append(words[row * NW + s])
+            res = apply_membership_words(vec, tuple(ws), n_cols=N)
+        for i in cutlass.range_constexpr(N):
+            out[row * N + i] = res[i]
+
+    @cute.jit
+    def membership_host(scores, words, out, n_blocks, N: cutlass.Constexpr[int], NW: cutlass.Constexpr[int], stream: cuda.CUstream):
+        membership_kernel(scores, words, out, N, NW).launch(grid=(n_blocks, 1, 1), block=(128, 1, 1), stream=stream)
+
+    def fake_1d(dtype):
+        """A fake 1-D tensor of ``dtype`` (symbolic length, 16-B aligned) for ``cute.compile``."""
+        return make_fake_tensor(dtype, (cute.sym_int(),), (1,), assumed_align=16)
+
+    def compile_membership(N: int, NW: int):
+        """Compile the probe for an ``N``-wide chunk over ``NW`` words."""
+        return cute.compile(
+            membership_host,
+            fake_1d(cutlass.Float32),
+            fake_1d(cutlass.Int32),
+            fake_1d(cutlass.Float32),
+            cutlass.Int32(0),
+            N,
+            NW,
+            make_fake_stream(use_tvm_ffi_env_stream=False),
+            options="--enable-tvm-ffi",
+        )
+
+    return compile_membership
+
+
+# ============================================================================ trace-time contracts (no device)
+def test_apply_membership_chunk_rejects_a_chunk_wider_than_two_words():
+    """``apply_membership_chunk`` serves 1..64 columns (two words); a wider chunk is refused by value."""
+    from cudnn.frost.tile_dsl.mask import apply_membership_chunk
+
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="n must be in 1..64"):
+        apply_membership_chunk(None, None, None, n=65)
+
+
+def test_apply_membership_words_rejects_too_few_words_for_the_chunk():
+    """``apply_membership_words`` refuses a word list that covers fewer columns than the chunk."""
+    from cudnn.frost.tile_dsl.mask import apply_membership_words
+
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="2 word\\(s\\) cover 64 columns, chunk has 96"):
+        apply_membership_words(None, (None, None), n_cols=96)
+
+
+# ============================================================================ numerics (any CUDA device)
+def _reference(scores: torch.Tensor, words: torch.Tensor, N: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """torch twin of the membership mask: keep ``scores[c]`` iff bit ``c % 32`` of word ``c // 32`` is set, else ``-inf``."""
+    bits = torch.arange(N, device=scores.device)
+    w = words.to(torch.int64) & 0xFFFFFFFF  # [rows, NW] as unsigned
+    sel = w[:, bits // 32]  # [rows, N]
+    keep = ((sel >> (bits % 32)) & 1) == 1
+    return torch.where(keep, scores, torch.full_like(scores, float("-inf")))
+
+
+@requires_sm80
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("N, NW", [(64, 2), (32, 1), (128, 4)], ids=["chunk64", "chunk32", "words128"])
+def test_apply_membership_matches_torch(N, NW):
+    """Cell ``i`` keeps ``S[i]`` iff bit ``i`` of the word table is set, else ``-inf``; planted rows: nothing kept, everything
+    kept, cell 0 only, the top cell only (bit 31 of the last word, signed), a NaN payload in a kept cell."""
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    dev = torch.device("cuda")
+    n_blocks, rows = 3, 3 * 128
+    scores = torch.randn(rows, N, device=dev, dtype=torch.float32)
+    words = torch.randint(-(2**31), 2**31 - 1, (rows, NW), device=dev, dtype=torch.int64).to(torch.int32)
+    words[0] = 0  # nothing kept
+    words[1] = -1  # everything kept (all ones)
+    words[2] = 0
+    words[2, 0] = 1  # only cell 0
+    words[3] = 0
+    words[3, NW - 1] = -(2**31)  # only cell N - 1 (bit 31 of the last word, the signed encoding)
+    words[4] = -1
+    scores[4, 5] = float("nan")  # a kept NaN passes through bit-exactly
+    out = torch.full_like(scores, 12345.0)
+    compile_membership = _probe()
+    art = compile_membership(N, NW)
+    import cutlass
+
+    art(scores.reshape(-1), words.reshape(-1), out.reshape(-1), cutlass.Int32(n_blocks), _stream())
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    want = _reference(scores, words, N)
+    assert torch.equal(out.view(torch.int32), want.view(torch.int32)), "bitwise, NaN payloads compared as bit patterns"
+    assert bool(torch.isinf(out[0]).all()) and bool((out[0] < 0).all())
+    assert torch.equal(out[1].view(torch.int32), scores[1].view(torch.int32))
+    assert out[2, 0] == scores[2, 0] and bool(torch.isinf(out[2, 1:]).all())
+    assert out[3, N - 1] == scores[3, N - 1] and bool(torch.isinf(out[3, : N - 1]).all())
+    assert bool(torch.isnan(out[4, 5]))

+"""``tile_dsl.barrier.arrive_on_leader_release`` / ``Producer.LEADER_RELEASE`` -- the cross-CTA arrive that PUBLISHES
+generic SMEM stores to the leader.
+
+``arrive_on_leader`` is ``relaxed=True`` at cluster scope: right when the data it publishes is an async-proxy TMEM write
+already completed by ``tcgen05_wait(STORE)``.  A follower that writes an MMA operand into ITS OWN
+SMEM with generic stores (``store_swizzled``), fences it into the async proxy and hands it to a leader-issued
+``cta_group::2`` MMA needs the arrive to RELEASE those stores to the leader's acquiring wait, or the MMA may read the
+slab stale -- a load-dependent first-launch race.  The
+form is ``mbarrier.arrive.release.cta.shared::cluster.b64`` on the mapa'd leader mbar (the DSL's own default for a remote
+arrive and the SM100 dkdv chain's ``producer_commit``), NEVER ``.release.cluster``: that puts a ``MEMBAR.ALL.GPU`` +
+``CGAERRBAR`` drain ahead of every arrive (removing that drain took a cga2 kernel from 47 % to 92 % of SOL).
+
+Tiers, one probe (2 CTAs x 32 lanes; every lane writes a pattern into its CTA's slab, fences, arrives on the leader's
+mbar; the leader waits and reads the FOLLOWER's slab over DSMEM):
+
+* tier 1 (any box whose cutlass-dsl knows ``sm_107a``): the trace-compile is asserted; the PTX carries exactly ONE
+  ``mbarrier.arrive.release.cta.shared::cluster.b64`` for the release form (zero ``.release.cluster``), the relaxed
+  control keeps its ``.relaxed.cluster`` form, the cga1 form falls through to a plain local arrive; with a decoding
+  nvdisasm the SASS of every form has ``CGAERRBAR == 0`` and ``MEMBAR.ALL.GPU == 0`` (the drain the rule forbids).
+* tier 2 (``requires_rubin``): the probe RUNS -- the leader reads the follower's 32-lane pattern exactly, for the release
+  form, the relaxed control and the cga1 form (a single-launch smoke of the publish-then-read shape; the 12-process x
+  {relaxed, release} x {follower delay} micro-probe under an async-proxy consumer belongs with the first kernel that
+  consumes the release arrive).
+
+The two ``mbar_arrive_on_peer(..., release_cta=True)`` arms ride the same probe (forms ``peer_release`` / ``peer_release_pred``): the
+UNPREDICATED arm (``mbarrier_arrive(mapa(mb, peer), scope=CTA, relaxed=False)``, no kernel calls it today -- pinned here so it cannot
+rot unseen) and the predicated inline-PTX arm (the multicast bias ring's cross-CTA stage credit, one elected lane per warp; its kernel
+module pins the rendering, this module pins the helper).  Both must read exactly one ``.release.cta.shared::cluster`` arrive, zero
+relaxed, zero ``.release.cluster``, and no GPU-scope drain in SASS; the probe also prints every ``SYNCS.ARRIVE`` mnemonic it decodes
+(``SASS_ARRIVE_MNEMONICS``), because the suffix is the lowering shape, not the memory order.

+    """Probe: 2 CTAs x 32 lanes; each lane stores a pattern into its CTA's SMEM slab, fences, arrives on the LEADER's
+    mbar (32 x 2 = 64 arrives); the leader waits and copies the follower's slab (DSMEM read) to GMEM."""

+
+    LANES = 32
+    FORM_RELEASE, FORM_RELAXED, FORM_CGA1, FORM_PEER_RELEASE, FORM_PEER_RELEASE_PRED = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4
+
+
+    @cute.kernel
+    def probe(mOut: cute.Tensor, form: cutlass.Constexpr[int]):
+        cta_group = 1 if form == FORM_CGA1 else 2
+        producer = Producer.LEADER if form in (FORM_RELAXED, FORM_CGA1) else Producer.LEADER_RELEASE
+        # the predicated peer form fires ONE elected lane per warp (one warp per CTA here); every other form arrives bare on all 32 lanes
+        arrivers = 1 if form == FORM_PEER_RELEASE_PRED else LANES
+        tidx = cutlass.Int32(cute.arch.thread_idx()[0])
+        cta = cutlass.Int32(cute.arch.block_idx_in_cluster()) if cutlass.const_expr(cta_group == 2) else cutlass.Int32(0)
+        slab = cutlass.Array(cutlass.Int32, LANES, alignment=16, space=cutlass.AddressSpace.smem)
+        bar_raw = cutlass.Array(cutlass.Int64, 1, alignment=8, space=cutlass.AddressSpace.smem)
+        # init count = SUM(issuing lanes): arrivers x cta_group CTAs (32 bare lanes, or the one elected lane of the predicated peer form)
+        bar = MBarrier(base_ptr=bar_raw, stages=1, init_count=arrivers * cta_group, producer=int(producer), scope=int(Scope.LEADER))
+        if tidx == 0:
+            bar.init()
+        nvvm.fence_mbarrier_init()
+        nvvm.barrier_cta_sync()
+        if cutlass.const_expr(cta_group == 2):
+            cga_arrive()
+            cga_wait()
+        # the follower's generic store of "its MMA operand", then the production recipe: fence into the async proxy, arrive
+        slab.subview(tidx).store(cta * cutlass.Int32(1000) + tidx * cutlass.Int32(7) + cutlass.Int32(1))
+        nvvm.fence_proxy("async.shared", space="cta")
+        if cutlass.const_expr(form == FORM_PEER_RELEASE):
+            # mbar_arrive_on_peer(release_cta=True) UNPREDICATED = mbarrier_arrive(mapa(mb, 0), scope=CTA, relaxed=False); no kernel caller today
+            bar.arrive_on_peer(cutlass.Int32(0), release_cta=True)
+        elif cutlass.const_expr(form == FORM_PEER_RELEASE_PRED):
+            # the multicast bias ring's stage credit: the predicated inline-PTX .release.cta arrive from one elected lane per warp
+            bar.arrive_on_peer(cutlass.Int32(0), pred=nvvm.elect_sync(), release_cta=True)
+        else:
+            bar.arrive(cta_group=cta_group, leader_cta_id=cutlass.Int32(0))
+        if cta == 0:
+            bar.wait(0)
+            # the leader reads the PEER's slab (cga2: CTA 1; cga1: mapa(self, 0) is the local slab)
+            peer_elem = nvvm.mapa(slab.subview(tidx), cutlass.Int32(cta_group - 1))
+            v = nvvm.inline_ptx("ld.shared::cluster.b32 $0, [$1];", write_only_types=[cutlass.Int32], read_only_args=[peer_elem.ir_value()])
+            st_global(mOut.iterator.toint() + tidx.to(cutlass.Int64) * cutlass.Int64(4), v, cutlass.Int32)
+        else:
+            # the follower publishes its own slab from a local read as the control row
+            st_global(mOut.iterator.toint() + cutlass.Int64(LANES * 4) + tidx.to(cutlass.Int64) * cutlass.Int64(4), slab.subview(tidx).load(), cutlass.Int32)
+        if cutlass.const_expr(cta_group == 2):
+            # P15: the follower must stay resident until the leader has read its SMEM
+            cga_arrive()
+            cga_wait()
+
+
+    probe.set_name_prefix("cudnn", remove_cutlass_symbol=True)
+
+
+    @cute.jit
+    def launch(out: cute.Tensor, form: cutlass.Constexpr[int], stream: cuda.CUstream):
+        if cutlass.const_expr(form == FORM_CGA1):
+            probe(out, form).launch(grid=(1, 1, 1), block=(LANES, 1, 1), stream=stream)
+        else:
+            probe(out, form).launch(grid=(2, 1, 1), block=(LANES, 1, 1), cluster=(2, 1, 1), stream=stream)
+
+
+    if __name__ == "__main__":
+        # argv: <arch> <form 0/1/2> <dump dir> [nvdisasm candidates...]; CUTE_DSL_DUMP_DIR is set by the caller (keeps ptx + cubin).
+        import glob, os, subprocess, sys
+        from cutlass.cute.runtime import make_fake_stream, make_fake_tensor
+
+        arch, form, dump, cands = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2]), sys.argv[3], sys.argv[4:]
+        out = make_fake_tensor(dtype=cutlass.Int32, shape=(cute.sym_int(),), stride=(1,), assumed_align=16)
+        cute.compile(launch, out, form, make_fake_stream(use_tvm_ffi_env_stream=False), options=f"--enable-tvm-ffi --gpu-arch {arch} --keep-cubin --keep-ptx")
+        print("COMPILED", arch, form)
+        ptxs = glob.glob(os.path.join(dump, f"*.{arch}.ptx"))
+        if not ptxs:
+            print("FAIL no ptx landed in", dump, os.listdir(dump)); sys.exit(3)
+        ptx = open(ptxs[0]).read()
+        for key, pat in (("RELEASE_CTA_CLUSTER", "mbarrier.arrive.release.cta.shared::cluster.b64"),
+                         ("RELEASE_CLUSTER_CLUSTER", "mbarrier.arrive.release.cluster.shared::cluster.b64"),
+                         ("RELAXED_CLUSTER_CLUSTER", "mbarrier.arrive.relaxed.cluster.shared::cluster.b64"),
+                         ("ANY_CLUSTER_ARRIVE", "shared::cluster.b64 _"),
+                         ("LOCAL_ARRIVE", "mbarrier.arrive.shared")):
+            print("PTX", key, ptx.count(pat))
+        cubins = glob.glob(os.path.join(dump, f"*.{arch}.cubin"))
+        if not cubins:
+            print("FAIL no cubin landed in", dump); sys.exit(3)
+        sass = None
+        for nvd in cands:
+            try:
+                proc = subprocess.run([nvd, "-c", cubins[0]], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120)
+            except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as exc:
+                print("REJECT", nvd, "->", repr(exc)); continue
+            if proc.returncode == 0 and proc.stdout.strip():
+                sass = proc.stdout.splitlines(); print("NVDISASM", nvd); break
+            print("REJECT", nvd, "->", (proc.stderr.strip().splitlines() or [str(proc.returncode)])[-1])
+        if sass is None:
+            print("SKIP no nvdisasm candidate decodes", arch); sys.exit(0)
+        print("SASS CGAERRBAR", sum(1 for ln in sass if "CGAERRBAR" in ln))
+        print("SASS MEMBAR_GPU", sum(1 for ln in sass if "MEMBAR.ALL.GPU" in ln))
+        print("SASS MEMBAR", sum(1 for ln in sass if "MEMBAR" in ln))
+        print("SASS ARRIVE", sum(1 for ln in sass if "SYNCS.ARRIVE" in ln))
+        print("SASS LINES", len(sass))
+        import re
+        mnem = sorted({m.group(0) for ln in sass for m in [re.search(r"U?SYNCS\\.ARRIVE[\\w.]*", ln)] if m})
+        print("SASS_ARRIVE_MNEMONICS", " ".join(mnem) if mnem else "none")
+    ''')
+
+
+def _write_probe(tmp_path):
+    probe_py = tmp_path / "release_arrive_probe.py"
+    probe_py.write_text(_PROBE_SRC)
+    return probe_py
+
+
+def _run_probe(tmp_path, *, arch: str, form: int, timeout: int = 900):
+    dump = tmp_path / f"dump_{arch}_{form}"
+    dump.mkdir()
+    env = dict(os.environ, CUTE_DSL_DUMP_DIR=str(dump), CUTE_DSL_KEEP="ptx,cubin")
+    argv = [sys.executable, str(_write_probe(tmp_path)), arch, str(form), str(dump), *nvdisasm_candidates()]
+    return subprocess.run(argv, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout, env=env)
+
+
+def _parse(lines):
+    ptx = {ln.split()[1]: int(ln.split()[2]) for ln in lines if ln.startswith("PTX ") and len(ln.split()) == 3}
+    sass = {ln.split()[1]: int(ln.split()[2]) for ln in lines if ln.startswith("SASS ") and len(ln.split()) == 3}
+    return ptx, sass
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Tier 1: PTX form + SASS drain pins on an sm_107a trace-compile
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("form_name", list(FORMS))
+def test_sm107a_release_arrive_ptx_form_and_no_gpu_drain(tmp_path, form_name):
+    """release / peer_release / peer_release_pred -> exactly one ``mbarrier.arrive.release.cta.shared::cluster.b64`` and NO
+    ``.release.cluster`` (the two ``mbar_arrive_on_peer(release_cta=True)`` arms, unpredicated and predicated, read the same form as
+    ``arrive_on_leader_release``); relaxed -> the ``.relaxed.cluster`` form (the ``arrive_on_leader`` control, untouched); cga1 -> a
+    plain local arrive and no cluster arrive at all.  With a decoding nvdisasm: ``CGAERRBAR == 0`` and ``MEMBAR.ALL.GPU == 0`` for
+    every form, and the decoded ``SYNCS.ARRIVE`` mnemonics are printed (``-s``) for the record."""
+    if not arch_known_to_the_dsl("sm_107a"):
+        pytest.skip("this cutlass-dsl has no sm_107a (needs >= 4.8.0)")
+    form = FORMS[form_name]
+    proc = _run_probe(tmp_path, arch="sm_107a", form=form)
+    assert proc.returncode == 0, f"sm_107a trace-compile of the {form_name} probe failed:\n{proc.stdout[-3000:]}\n{proc.stderr[-3000:]}"
+    lines = proc.stdout.splitlines()
+    assert any(ln.startswith("COMPILED sm_107a") for ln in lines), proc.stdout[-2000:]
+    ptx, sass = _parse(lines)
+    mnem = [ln for ln in lines if ln.startswith("SASS_ARRIVE_MNEMONICS")]
+    print(f"\n[{form_name}] PTX {ptx} SASS {sass} {mnem[0] if mnem else ''}")
+    assert ptx["RELEASE_CLUSTER_CLUSTER"] == 0, f"a .release.cluster arrive is a MEMBAR.ALL.GPU + CGAERRBAR drain per arrive -- {ptx}"
+    if form in RELEASE_FORMS:
+        assert ptx["RELEASE_CTA_CLUSTER"] == 1 and ptx["RELAXED_CLUSTER_CLUSTER"] == 0, ptx
+    elif form == FORM_RELAXED:
+        assert ptx["RELAXED_CLUSTER_CLUSTER"] == 1 and ptx["RELEASE_CTA_CLUSTER"] == 0, ptx
+    else:
+        assert ptx["ANY_CLUSTER_ARRIVE"] == 0 and ptx["LOCAL_ARRIVE"] >= 1, f"cga1 must fall through to a plain local arrive -- {ptx}"
+    if not nvdisasm_candidates():
+        pytest.skip("compiled + PTX pinned; no nvdisasm executable to try for the SASS half (CUDA_PATH unset and none on PATH)")
+    if any(ln.startswith("SKIP") for ln in lines):
+        pytest.skip(f"compiled + PTX pinned; SASS half skipped: {[ln for ln in lines if ln.startswith(('SKIP', 'REJECT'))]}")
+    assert sass["CGAERRBAR"] == 0 and sass["MEMBAR_GPU"] == 0, f"{form_name}: a GPU-scope drain sits before the cluster arrive -- {sass}"
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Tier 2: the publish-then-read runs on a Rubin device
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+@requires_rubin
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("form_name", list(FORMS))
+def test_leader_reads_the_followers_slab_after_the_arrive(tmp_path, form_name):
+    """The leader's 32 lanes read the follower's pattern ``1000 + 7 * lane + 1`` exactly (cga2 -- the release form, the relaxed
+    control and both ``arrive_on_peer(release_cta=True)`` arms), or their own ``7 * lane + 1`` at cga1; the follower's control row is
+    its own slab."""
+    import cuda.bindings.driver as _cuda_driver
+    import cutlass.cute as cute
+    from cutlass.cute.runtime import from_dlpack
+
+    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("_release_arrive_probe_device", str(_write_probe(tmp_path)))
+    mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+    spec.loader.exec_module(mod)
+    form = FORMS[form_name]
+    dev = torch.device("cuda")
+    out = torch.full((2 * LANES,), -1, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
+    stream = _cuda_driver.CUstream(torch.cuda.current_stream(dev).cuda_stream)
+    arg = from_dlpack(out, assumed_align=16)
+    fn = cute.compile(mod.launch, arg, form, stream)
+    fn(arg, stream)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    lane = torch.arange(LANES, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
+    if form == FORM_CGA1:
+        expect_leader = 7 * lane + 1
+        assert torch.equal(out[:LANES], expect_leader), out[:LANES].tolist()
+    else:
+        expect_leader = 1000 + 7 * lane + 1
+        assert torch.equal(out[:LANES], expect_leader), f"leader read of the follower's slab: {out[:LANES].tolist()}"
+        assert torch.equal(out[LANES:], expect_leader), f"follower control row: {out[LANES:].tolist()}"
